**[soft-edge-content-fade](https://github.com/GoogleChrome/modern-web-guidance/blob/main/skills/modern-web-guidance/guides/visual-design/soft-edge-content-fade.md)**: Apply a transparency gradient to content edges to indicate further scrollable areas or to obscure payment-walled text. - **[typography](https://github.com/GoogleChrome/modern-web-guidance/blob/main/skills/modern-web-guidance/guides/visual-design/typography.md)**: Typography best practices for the web, including font sizing units, line height, text wrapping and balancing, and fluid type that scales with the viewport. - **[visual-effects](https://github.com/GoogleChrome/modern-web-guidance/blob/main/skills/modern-web-guidance/guides/visual-design/visual-effects.md)**: Visual effects with CSS such as layered shadows, blend modes, gradients with predictable color interpolation, and patterns like stripes, checkerboards, dots, and pie charts built from gradients alone. - **[visually-stable-font-fallbacks](https://github.com/GoogleChrome/modern-web-guidance/blob/main/skills/modern-web-guidance/guides/visual-design/visually-stable-font-fallbacks.md)**: Define font styles such that text remains readable and visually consistent in the event that there's a swap between the preferred font and one of the fallbacks (or vice versa). - **[visually-stable-mixed-fonts](https://github.com/GoogleChrome/modern-web-guidance/blob/main/skills/modern-web-guidance/guides/visual-design/visually-stable-mixed-fonts.md)**: Define font styles such that text remains readable and visually consistent in situations where multiple fonts are used to render a single block of text. - **[visually-texture-content](https://github.com/GoogleChrome/modern-web-guidance/blob/main/skills/modern-web-guidance/guides/visual-design/visually-texture-content.md)**: Apply realistic weathering and texture patterns to elements to give them an organic, aged, or physical material appearance.

wasm

- **[cpp-on-the-web](https://github.com/GoogleChrome/modern-web-guidance/blob/main/skills/modern-web-guidance/guides/wasm/cpp-on-the-web.md)**: Compile C/C++ to WebAssembly using Emscripten

webmcp

- **[agentic-forms](https://github.com/GoogleChrome/modern-web-guidance/blob/main/skills/modern-web-guidance/guides/webmcp/agentic-forms.md)**: Expose client-side functionality as tools to AI agents by annotating standard HTML forms with WebMCP attributes. - **[agentic-javascript-tools](https://github.com/GoogleChrome/modern-web-guidance/blob/main/skills/modern-web-guidance/guides/webmcp/agentic-javascript-tools.md)**: Programmatically register client-side JavaScript functions as tools for AI agents using the WebMCP Imperative API. - **[webmcp](https://github.com/GoogleChrome/modern-web-guidance/blob/main/skills/modern-web-guidance/guides/webmcp/webmcp.md)**: Use this guide to implement WebMCP in browser applications, exposing client-side functionality as tools to AI agents via declarative or imperative APIs.
### Safe Adoption of Modern Features * **Progressive Enhancement & Nuanced Fallbacks**: We distinguish between purely additive enhancements (like speculative preloading) which are safe to let older browsers silently ignore, and critical behaviors (like dialog controls or network beacons) where we write highly considered, low-overhead fallbacks. * **Responsible Fallbacks**: We prioritize lightweight, case-specific custom fallbacks (<50 LOC) or conditionally-loaded polyfills instead of heavy third-party bundles. * **Gotchas & Quirks**: We document hidden platform limitations, such as the 64KB payload quota for `fetchLater()` or macOS-specific scrollbar behaviors. * **Baseline-Aware Integration**: We leverage real-time compatibility data from the **Baseline** project so agents dynamically adapt to current browser support. * **Origin Trial & Volatile Feature Gates**: Guides covering experimental **Origin Trial** APIs or **volatile features** (single-engine features shipped within the last 3 months or still stabilizing) remain discoverable via `search`, but are gated on `retrieve` so agents do not adopt unstable APIs without explicit developer consent. ### Project Configuration (`.mwgrc`) Configure Origin Trial and volatile feature opt-ins for a repository with an optional `.mwgrc` JSON file in your project root (or `~/.mwgrc` as a user-level fallback), which you can commit to share across your team: | CLI Command | `.mwgrc` Key | Effect | | :--- | :--- | :--- | | `npx modern-web-guidance@latest set-allow-origin-trials` | `"allowOriginTrials": true` | Unlocks guides for experimental Origin Trial APIs. | | `npx modern-web-guidance@latest set-allow-volatile-features` | `"allowVolatileFeatures": true` | Unlocks guides for volatile single-engine features. | ## How It Works 1. **Activation**: The coding agent activates the `modern-web-guidance` skill because of a relevant task. The agent is instructed to use the `modern-web-guidance` CLI for web platform queries. 2. **Local Semantic Search**: The agent runs `modern-web-guidance search ""`. The tool matches the query to the best guide using an offline, zero-dependency embedding model and BM25 search engine (no network calls, no API keys). 3. **Guide Fetch**: The agent retrieves the guide via `modern-web-guidance retrieve `, inserting targeted code patterns, gotchas, and fallbacks directly into its context window. > [!TIP] > Note: We use `npx` to ensure the content doesn't go stale, but the CLI works offline, completely private and local. > The npm package is self-contained, with no extra dependencies to ensure both low-latency and supply-chain security. ## Alternative Installation Methods
Vercel Skills CLI (aka npx skills) ```shell npx skills add GoogleChrome/modern-web-guidance ```
GitHub CLI ```shell gh skill install GoogleChrome/modern-web-guidance ```
Google Antigravity ```shell agy plugin install https://github.com/GoogleChrome/modern-web-guidance ```
GitHub Copilot CLI ```shell /plugin marketplace add GoogleChrome/modern-web-guidance /plugin install modern-web-guidance@googlechrome ```
Claude Code Plugin ```shell /plugin marketplace add GoogleChrome/modern-web-guidance /plugin install modern-web-guidance@googlechrome /plugin # Select GoogleChrome marketplace, press enter, enable AutoUpdate /reload-plugins ```
Grok Build CLI ```shell grok plugin install https://github.com/GoogleChrome/modern-web-guidance --trust ```
Kimi Code ```shell /plugins install https://github.com/GoogleChrome/modern-web-guidance ```
OpenAI Codex ```shell codex plugin marketplace add GoogleChrome/modern-web-guidance codex plugin add modern-web-guidance@googlechrome ```
## Updating If you installed the skill using `npx modern-web-guidance@latest install`, you can update with: `npx modern-web-guidance@latest update`. Otherwise, consult your agent's documentation for updating plugins and skills. ## Evals to prove this works well We developed a robust eval harness to ensure that the content is **empirically proven and continuously calibrated** so AI agents write better code. We run automated evaluations using a closed-loop validation pipeline: ``` [ Expert-authored guidance and demo ] │ ▼ [ Target generation ] ──> Tasks on real webapps, Golden solutions, Playwright graders │ ▼ [ Calibration loop ] ───> Runs Grader on Golden Solutions (Must Pass 100%) │ Runs Grader on Unmodified Base App (Must Fail 100%) ▼ [ E2E agent evals ] ────> Runs coding agents in guided vs. unguided modes Compares pass rates and accessibility w/ and w/o the skill ``` 1. **Simulated Developer Tasks**: We define realistic developer prompts against full base applications (`daily-grind`, `devtools-times`) that mimic real-world requests (e.g., "make my images load faster"). Prompts avoid naming APIs or features, testing whether the agent can naturally discover and apply the right guides. 2. **Static & Browser-Based Assertions**: Playwright graders verify that each implementation requirement was followed—checking source patterns, computed styles, runtime DOM behaviors, and accessibility states. 3. **Self-Healing Calibration**: Graders are calibrated against multi-agent (Claude/Codex/AGY) golden solutions (100% pass target) and an unmodified baseline application (0% pass target). 4. **E2E Testing**: We measure coding agent performance on real tasks with and without guidance. The _opportunity_ (100% - unguided pass rate) and _uplift_ (guided - unguided pass rate) are key: if models already succeed without guidance, we prune redundant advice; where agents struggle, we refine guides to maximize uplift. ### Recent eval results snapshot Explore full per-agent and per-guide breakdowns on the **[Eval Dashboard](https://googlechrome.github.io/modern-web-guidance-src/)**. | Date | Agent + Model | Tasks / Assertions | Unguided → Guided (Uplift) | | :--- | :--- | :---: | :---: | | Nov 8 | antigravity_cli (gemini-4-argon) | 214 / 1673 | 58% → 94% (**+36pp**) | | Nov 8 | codex_cli (gpt-6.1-sol) | 215 / 1795 | 54% → 82% (**+28pp**) | | Nov 8 | claude_code (opus-5-5) | 215 / 1801 | 57% → 88% (**+31pp**) | | Nov 6 | codex_cli (gpt-6.1-sol) | 212 / 1773 | 53% → 86% (**+33pp**) | | Nov 6 | claude_code (opus-5-5) | 212 / 1773 | 56% → 90% (**+34pp**) | | Nov 6 | antigravity_cli (gemini-4-argon) | 212 / 1722 | 60% → 96% (**+36pp**) | | Nov 4 | codex_cli (gpt-6.1-sol) | 209 / 1743 | 52% → 85% (**+33pp**) | | Nov 4 | claude_code (opus-5-5) | 209 / 1743 | 57% → 90% (**+33pp**) | | Nov 4 | antigravity_cli (gemini-4-argon) | 207 / 1722 | 60% → 96% (**+36pp**) | | Nov 2 | codex_cli (gpt-6.1-sol) | 205 / 1729 | 55% → 82% (**+27pp**) | ## Available Skill Packs You can customize which skill packs are installed using the `--choose` flag: ```shell npx modern-web-guidance@latest install --choose ``` * **`modern-web-guidance`** (~205 tokens): Comprehensive guidance on modern browser APIs, layouts, and performance. * **`chrome-extensions`** (~175 tokens): Guidance on Manifest V3, background workers, extension APIs, and Chrome Web Store publishing. ## Telemetry & Privacy Google collects anonymous usage information to improve the tool's reliability, relevance, and performance. Collected information includes installation counts, the calling agent name, guide retrieval IDs, and CLI tool search queries generated by the agent (e.g. "dark mode scrollbar color-scheme"). Raw user prompts are not collected. You can inspect what is collected in [modern-web.ts](https://github.com/GoogleChrome/modern-web-guidance-src/blob/main/src/cli/modern-web.ts). > [!TIP] > **To Opt-Out:** set the `DISABLE_TELEMETRY=1` env variable in your shell profile (e.g., `.bashrc` or `.zshrc`): > ```bash > export DISABLE_TELEMETRY=1 > ``` Google handles this data in accordance with the [Google Privacy Policy](https://policies.google.com/privacy). ## Contributors Found a bug, outdated pattern, or missing web platform feature? [Open an issue](https://github.com/GoogleChrome/modern-web-guidance-src/issues) or see [`CONTRIBUTING.md`](https://github.com/GoogleChrome/modern-web-guidance-src/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) in the [source repository (`GoogleChrome/modern-web-guidance-src`)](https://github.com/GoogleChrome/modern-web-guidance-src). Huge thanks to everyone who has contributed! ## License Unless otherwise noted: * Software code in this project is licensed under the [Apache License 2.0](https://github.com/GoogleChrome/modern-web-guidance-src/blob/main/LICENSE). * Documentation and guide content under `guides/` are licensed under [Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International (CC-BY 4.0)](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Portions of the documentation in this project are derived from [MDN Web Docs](https://developer.mozilla.org/) by Mozilla Contributors and [W3C](https://www.w3.org/), [WHATWG](https://whatwg.org), and [IETF](https://www.ietf.org) specifications.

repositories.description: An open-source remote desktop application designed for self-hosting, as an alternative to TeamViewer.
repositories.readme:
Build • Docker • Structure • Screenshots
[Українська] | [česky] | [中文] | [Magyar] | [Español] | [فارسی] | [Français] | [Deutsch] | [Polski] | [Indonesian] | [Suomi] | [മലയാളം] | [日本語] | [Nederlands] | [Italiano] | [Русский] | [Português (Portugal)] | [Português (Brasil)] | [Esperanto] | [한국어] | [العربي] | [Tiếng Việt] | [Dansk] | [Ελληνικά] | [Türkçe] | [Norsk] | [Română]
We need your help to translate this README, RustDesk UI and RustDesk Doc to your native language

> [!Caution] > **Misuse Disclaimer:**
> The developers of RustDesk do not condone or support any unethical or illegal use of this software. Misuse, such as unauthorized access, control or invasion of privacy, is strictly against our guidelines. The authors are not responsible for any misuse of the application. Chat with us: [Discord](https://discord.gg/nDceKgxnkV) | [Twitter](https://twitter.com/rustdesk) | [Reddit](https://www.reddit.com/r/rustdesk) | [YouTube](https://www.youtube.com/@rustdesk) [![RustDesk Server Pro](https://img.shields.io/badge/RustDesk%20Server%20Pro-Advanced%20Features-blue)](https://rustdesk.com/pricing.html) Yet another remote desktop solution, written in Rust. Works out of the box with no configuration required. You have full control of your data, with no concerns about security. You can use our rendezvous/relay server, [set up your own](https://rustdesk.com/server), or [write your own rendezvous/relay server](https://github.com/rustdesk/rustdesk-server-demo). ![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/71636191/171661982-430285f0-2e12-4b1d-9957-4a58e375304d.png) RustDesk welcomes contribution from everyone. See [CONTRIBUTING.md](docs/CONTRIBUTING.md) for help getting started. [**FAQ**](https://github.com/rustdesk/rustdesk/wiki/FAQ) [**BINARY DOWNLOAD**](https://github.com/rustdesk/rustdesk/releases) [**NIGHTLY BUILD**](https://github.com/rustdesk/rustdesk/releases/tag/nightly) [](https://f-droid.org/en/packages/com.carriez.flutter_hbb) [](https://flathub.org/apps/com.rustdesk.RustDesk) ## Dependencies Desktop versions use Flutter or Sciter (deprecated) for GUI. This tutorial is for Sciter only, since it is easier and more friendly to start. Check out our [CI](https://github.com/rustdesk/rustdesk/blob/master/.github/workflows/flutter-build.yml) for building the Flutter version. Please download Sciter dynamic library yourself. [Windows](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/c-smile/sciter-sdk/master/bin.win/x64/sciter.dll) | [Linux](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/c-smile/sciter-sdk/master/bin.lnx/x64/libsciter-gtk.so) | [macOS](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/c-smile/sciter-sdk/master/bin.osx/libsciter.dylib) ## Raw Steps to build - Prepare your Rust development env and C++ build env - Install [vcpkg](https://github.com/microsoft/vcpkg), and set `VCPKG_ROOT` env variable correctly - Windows: vcpkg install libvpx:x64-windows-static libyuv:x64-windows-static opus:x64-windows-static aom:x64-windows-static - Linux/macOS: vcpkg install libvpx libyuv opus aom - run `cargo run` ## [Build](https://rustdesk.com/docs/en/dev/build/) ## How to Build on Linux ### Ubuntu 18 (Debian 10) ```sh sudo apt install -y zip g++ gcc git curl wget nasm yasm libgtk-3-dev clang libxcb-randr0-dev libxdo-dev \ libxfixes-dev libxcb-shape0-dev libxcb-xfixes0-dev libasound2-dev libpulse-dev cmake make \ libclang-dev ninja-build libgstreamer1.0-dev libgstreamer-plugins-base1.0-dev ``` ### openSUSE Tumbleweed ```sh sudo zypper install gcc-c++ git curl wget nasm yasm gcc gtk3-devel clang libxcb-devel libXfixes-devel cmake alsa-lib-devel gstreamer-devel gstreamer-plugins-base-devel xdotool-devel ``` ### Fedora 28 (CentOS 8) ```sh sudo yum -y install gcc-c++ git curl wget nasm yasm gcc gtk3-devel clang libxcb-devel libxdo-devel libXfixes-devel pulseaudio-libs-devel cmake alsa-lib-devel gstreamer1-devel gstreamer1-plugins-base-devel ``` ### Arch (Manjaro) ```sh sudo pacman -Syu --needed unzip git cmake gcc curl wget yasm nasm zip make pkg-config clang gtk3 xdotool libxcb libxfixes alsa-lib pipewire ``` ### Install vcpkg ```sh git clone https://github.com/microsoft/vcpkg cd vcpkg git checkout 2023.04.15 cd .. vcpkg/bootstrap-vcpkg.sh export VCPKG_ROOT=$HOME/vcpkg vcpkg/vcpkg install libvpx libyuv opus aom ``` ### Fix libvpx (For Fedora) ```sh cd vcpkg/buildtrees/libvpx/src cd * ./configure sed -i 's/CFLAGS+=-I/CFLAGS+=-fPIC -I/g' Makefile sed -i 's/CXXFLAGS+=-I/CXXFLAGS+=-fPIC -I/g' Makefile make cp libvpx.a $HOME/vcpkg/installed/x64-linux/lib/ cd ``` ### Build ```sh curl --proto '=https' --tlsv1.2 -sSf https://sh.rustup.rs | sh source $HOME/.cargo/env git clone --recurse-submodules https://github.com/rustdesk/rustdesk cd rustdesk mkdir -p target/debug wget https://raw.githubusercontent.com/c-smile/sciter-sdk/master/bin.lnx/x64/libsciter-gtk.so mv libsciter-gtk.so target/debug VCPKG_ROOT=$HOME/vcpkg cargo run ``` ## How to build with Docker Begin by cloning the repository and building the Docker container: ```sh git clone https://github.com/rustdesk/rustdesk cd rustdesk git submodule update --init --recursive docker build -t "rustdesk-builder" . ``` Then, each time you need to build the application, run the following command: ```sh docker run --rm -it -v $PWD:/home/user/rustdesk -v rustdesk-git-cache:/home/user/.cargo/git -v rustdesk-registry-cache:/home/user/.cargo/registry -e PUID="$(id -u)" -e PGID="$(id -g)" rustdesk-builder ``` Note that the first build may take longer before dependencies are cached, subsequent builds will be faster. Additionally, if you need to specify different arguments to the build command, you may do so at the end of the command in the `` position. For instance, if you wanted to build an optimized release version, you would run the command above followed by `--release`. The resulting executable will be available in the target folder on your system, and can be run with: ```sh target/debug/rustdesk ``` Or, if you're running a release executable: ```sh target/release/rustdesk ``` Please ensure that you run these commands from the root of the RustDesk repository, or the application may not find the required resources. Also note that other cargo subcommands such as `install` or `run` are not currently supported via this method as they would install or run the program inside the container instead of the host. ## File Structure - **[libs/hbb_common](https://github.com/rustdesk/rustdesk/tree/master/libs/hbb_common)**: video codec, config, tcp/udp wrapper, and some other utility functions shared with the server - **[libs/base](https://github.com/rustdesk/rustdesk/tree/master/libs/base)**: protobuf, fs functions for file transfer, keyboard and platform code used only by this app - **[libs/scrap](https://github.com/rustdesk/rustdesk/tree/master/libs/scrap)**: screen capture - **[libs/enigo](https://github.com/rustdesk/rustdesk/tree/master/libs/enigo)**: platform specific keyboard/mouse control - **[libs/clipboard](https://github.com/rustdesk/rustdesk/tree/master/libs/clipboard)**: file copy and paste implementation for Windows, Linux, macOS. - **[src/ui](https://github.com/rustdesk/rustdesk/tree/master/src/ui)**: obsolete Sciter UI (deprecated) - **[src/server](https://github.com/rustdesk/rustdesk/tree/master/src/server)**: audio/clipboard/input/video services, and network connections - **[src/client.rs](https://github.com/rustdesk/rustdesk/tree/master/src/client.rs)**: start a peer connection - **[src/rendezvous_mediator.rs](https://github.com/rustdesk/rustdesk/tree/master/src/rendezvous_mediator.rs)**: Communicate with [rustdesk-server](https://github.com/rustdesk/rustdesk-server), wait for remote direct (TCP hole punching) or relayed connection - **[src/platform](https://github.com/rustdesk/rustdesk/tree/master/src/platform)**: platform specific code - **[flutter](https://github.com/rustdesk/rustdesk/tree/master/flutter)**: Flutter code for desktop and mobile ## Screenshots ![Connection Manager](https://github.com/rustdesk/rustdesk/assets/28412477/db82d4e7-c4bc-4823-8e6f-6af7eadf7651) ![Connected to a Windows PC](https://github.com/rustdesk/rustdesk/assets/28412477/9baa91e9-3362-4d06-aa1a-7518edcbd7ea) ![File Transfer](https://github.com/rustdesk/rustdesk/assets/28412477/39511ad3-aa9a-4f8c-8947-1cce286a46ad) ![TCP Tunneling](https://github.com/rustdesk/rustdesk/assets/28412477/78e8708f-e87e-4570-8373-1360033ea6c5)

repositories.readme:
Build your own AI office with Univer Office SDK.

Start with open-source Sheets and Docs, then connect your own application or agent.

🚀 Quick start · 📚 Documentation · ⚖️ Feature comparison · 🌐 Website · 🎮 Showcase · 🔧 API Reference · 📝 Blog

English · Français · Deutsch · Español · 简体中文 · 繁體中文 · 日本語 · 한국어

Table of contents - [💡 What is Univer?](#what-is-univer) - [Open-source capabilities](#open-source-capabilities) - [🚀 Build on the open-source foundation](#what-you-can-build) - [Quick start: an open-source spreadsheet editor](#quick-start) - [Connect your application to editable content](#connect-your-application-to-editable-content) - [🏗️ Explore the open-source architecture](#open-source-architecture) - [Give custom features clear boundaries](#give-custom-features-clear-boundaries) - [Compose cross-feature edits and undo/redo](#compose-cross-feature-edits-and-undoredo) - [Connect applications and agents through Facade APIs and events](#connect-applications-and-agents-through-facade-apis-and-events) - [🧩 Extend your application with Univer Office SDK](#open-source-and-commercial-extensions) - [Scope and licensing](#scope-and-licensing) - [🌐 Application patterns and ecosystem](#application-patterns-and-ecosystem) - [Univer Workspace: an Office SDK reference application](#univer-workspace-an-office-sdk-reference-application) - [CLI, agent integrations, and developer skills](#cli-agent-integrations-and-developer-skills) - [📚 Documentation and contributing](#documentation-and-contributing) - [Runtime compatibility](#runtime-compatibility) - [💬 Community](#community) - [🔒 Security](#security) - [❤️ Sponsors](#sponsors) - [📄 License](#license)
## 💡 What is Univer?

**Univer** is an Office SDK for building Office applications inside your own product. It provides Office editing, calculation, collaboration, and file processing for people and existing agents, using your data and permissions. The product family covers spreadsheets, documents, presentations, relational tables, canvases, and PDFs. Univer Office SDK has three parts: - **Web SDK** is the foundation: content models, editing, rendering, formula calculation, and Facade APIs (application-facing APIs). Compose its plugins into an embedded editor or your own Office application, and reuse the content models, commands, and calculation for Headless processing without an interactive editor. - **Server SDK** adds backend services for real-time collaboration, edit history, and Office file import and export. - **AI SDK** connects Office capabilities to existing agents and workflows, with content tools, execution, and review integrations. **This repository provides the Web SDK's core architecture and engine implementations under Apache-2.0**: content models and snapshot formats, plugin and dependency management, the command system, formula and rendering engines, Facade APIs, UI foundation, and Sheets and Docs editing capabilities. Commercial Web SDK plugins, Server SDK, and commercial AI SDK extensions are distributed and licensed separately. Agents can use the same open-source APIs; your application supplies the model and tool orchestration. The [quotation example](#connect-your-application-to-editable-content) demonstrates editing, calculation, and saving without an AI SDK dependency. ### Open-source capabilities
Area Selected capabilities
Sheets · Editing and layout Cell styles, merged cells, in-cell rich text, freeze panes, floating images, and undo/redo.
Sheets · Data and calculation Formulas, defined names, filtering, sorting, data validation, conditional formatting, hyperlinks, comments, and find and replace.
Docs Rich-text editing, paragraph formatting, lists, hyperlinks, comments, and drawing integration.
Features are composed through plugins and presets; the [quick start](#quick-start) uses only the **Sheets Core preset**. Images use the corresponding drawing plugins. See the [feature comparison](https://univer.ai/compare/) for detailed open-source and commercial coverage. The demos below showcase the wider **Univer Office SDK**, including commercial capabilities. They show more than the default open-source setup; see [open source and commercial extensions](#open-source-and-commercial-extensions) for scope.

## 🚀 Build on the open-source foundation

Your goal Use the open-source foundation Start here
Embed Sheets or Docs Add an editable Office surface to your application or agent product, and connect your data through Facade APIs. Quick start
Process content without an editor Reuse content plugins, models, commands, and calculation in Node.js for editing, snapshots, and automated tasks. Headless guide
Develop custom features or editors Reuse the engines, UI components, plugin boundaries, dependency injection, and command/undo systems. Follow existing features to extend Sheets and Docs or develop your own editors. Open-source architecture
**Coordinate edits and undo/redo across features.** Inserting a row inside a filter range changes both the base content and the filter range; undo needs to restore both. Each feature supplies its own changes and undo data, and the command composes their execution and history. The architecture walkthrough explains how to extend these editing workflows. ### Quick start: an open-source spreadsheet editor In a browser application using a bundler such as Vite: ```bash pnpm add @univerjs/presets @univerjs/preset-sheets-core ``` Create the container before initializing Univer: ```html
``` ```ts import { UniverSheetsCorePreset } from '@univerjs/preset-sheets-core' import UniverPresetSheetsCoreEnUS from '@univerjs/preset-sheets-core/locales/en-US' import { createUniver, LocaleType, mergeLocales } from '@univerjs/presets' import '@univerjs/preset-sheets-core/lib/index.css' const { univerAPI } = createUniver({ locale: LocaleType.EN_US, locales: { [LocaleType.EN_US]: mergeLocales(UniverPresetSheetsCoreEnUS), }, presets: [ UniverSheetsCorePreset({ container: 'app', }), ], }) univerAPI.createWorkbook({}) ``` Your page now contains a spreadsheet editor. Use the returned `univerAPI` to work with its content. This example uses open-source packages and needs no commercial Univer license or Server SDK. For component frameworks, retain the `univer` instance returned by `createUniver` and call `univer.dispose()` when the component unmounts. See the [lifecycle guide](https://docs.univer.ai/guides/sheets/getting-started/lifecycle). Presets compose plugins and register their Facade APIs. For manual control, see the [Plugin Mode example](#manual-plugin-composition) below. The [installation guide](https://docs.univer.ai/guides/sheets/getting-started/installation) covers both modes, peer dependencies, and framework integrations. Keep coordinated `@univerjs/*` packages on the same version. Commercial packages must use the matching release line; independently released packages such as icons follow their declared compatibility. See the [API Stability Policy](./docs/API_STABILITY.md). ### Connect your application to editable content Facade APIs are the application-facing interface to workbooks, worksheets, and ranges. Continue from the quick start to populate a quotation, update a quantity from application code, and read the recalculated total: ```ts // Wait for formula controllers before editing a newly created workbook. await new Promise((resolve) => { if (univerAPI.getCurrentLifecycleStage() >= univerAPI.Enum.LifecycleStages.Steady) { resolve() return } const listener = univerAPI.addEvent(univerAPI.Event.LifeCycleChanged, ({ stage }) => { if (stage === univerAPI.Enum.LifecycleStages.Steady) { listener.dispose() resolve() } }) }) const workbook = univerAPI.getActiveWorkbook()! const sheet = workbook.getActiveSheet() sheet.getRange('A1:D4').setValues([ ['Item', 'Quantity', 'Unit price', 'Amount'], ['Seats', 2, 25, '=B2*C2'], ['Support', 1, 100, '=B3*C3'], ['Total', '', '', '=SUM(D2:D3)'], ]) // An application control or agent can make the same edit. sheet.getRange('B2').setValue(4) univerAPI.getFormula().onCalculationResultApplied().then(() => { console.log(sheet.getRange('D4').getValue()) // 200 localStorage.setItem('quotation', JSON.stringify(workbook.save())) }).catch(console.error) ``` The editor and your application operate on the same workbook; formula changes are recalculated automatically. `workbook.save()` returns a JSON snapshot containing the workbook and its registered plugin data. Your application owns persistence; this example uses browser storage. On a later page load, after initialization, restore the snapshot **instead of creating a blank workbook**: ```ts const saved = localStorage.getItem('quotation') if (saved) { univerAPI.createWorkbook(JSON.parse(saved)) } ``` This workflow uses only open-source packages. Snapshot persistence is separate from XLSX import and export, which uses the separately distributed file-conversion capabilities. Use public Facade APIs for application integration; the source links below explain internal implementation and extension points. See the [API Stability Policy](./docs/API_STABILITY.md) before depending on an extension point.
Advanced: compose plugins manually (Plugin Mode) Use Plugin Mode when you need precise control over plugin selection, dependencies, or loading. The preset above handles this composition for you. This alternative initialization uses the same `app` container and the Sheets Core preset's browser plugin stack without a Worker. Use it **instead of** the preset initialization, then run the same quotation example with the returned `univerAPI`. ```bash pnpm add @univerjs/core @univerjs/design @univerjs/docs @univerjs/docs-ui \ @univerjs/engine-formula @univerjs/engine-render @univerjs/network \ @univerjs/sheets @univerjs/sheets-ui @univerjs/sheets-formula \ @univerjs/sheets-formula-ui @univerjs/sheets-numfmt \ spreadsheet rich-text editing. When adding a feature, include its corresponding Facade extensions, locale bundles, and UI styles. Dispose `univer` when its container is unmounted.

## 🏗️ Explore the open-source architecture

### Give custom features clear boundaries Univer organizes content logic and UI interaction in separate plugins. Feature plugins manage rules and content changes; UI plugins provide the interface and user interactions. For example, `sheets-filter` manages filter ranges and rules, while `sheets-filter-ui` provides panels, menus, and shortcuts. ```mermaid %%{init: {'htmlLabels': false, 'theme': 'base', 'themeVariables': {'fontFamily': 'Arial, PingFang SC, Microsoft YaHei, sans-serif', 'fontSize': '17px', 'lineColor': '#64748b'}, 'flowchart': {'htmlLabels': false, 'curve': 'linear', 'nodeSpacing': 28, 'rankSpacing': 45, 'padding': 16, 'wrappingWidth': 270}}}%% %% A layered overview, not a complete dependency graph. %% Group arrows indicate reuse of the layer below; internal arrows show selected dependencies. flowchart TD subgraph FEATURES["Feature Plugins"] direction LR FUI["Filter
UI Plugin"] VUI["Data Validation
UI Plugin"] FILTER["Filter Plugin"] VALIDATION["Data Validation Plugin"] FUI --> FILTER VUI --> VALIDATION end subgraph PRODUCTS["Product Plugins"] direction LR SUI["Sheets UI Plugin"] SHEETS["Sheets Plugin"] SUI --> SHEETS end subgraph FOUNDATION["Core Framework & Plugins"] direction LR UI["UI Plugin"] FORMULA["Formula Engine Plugin"] RENDER["Render Engine Plugin"] CORE["Core"] UI --> RENDER RENDER --> CORE FORMULA --> CORE end FEATURES --> PRODUCTS PRODUCTS --> FOUNDATION classDef logic fill:#eff6ff,color:#17365f,stroke:#93b4df,stroke-width:1.5px classDef ui fill:#f0fdf4,color:#17543a,stroke:#91c8a7,stroke-width:1.5px classDef shared fill:#f6f7f9,color:#334155,stroke:#bac3ce,stroke-width:1.5px classDef feature fill:#172d50,color:#ffffff,stroke:#172d50 class FUI,VUI ui class FILTER,VALIDATION logic class SUI,SHEETS logic class UI,FORMULA,RENDER,CORE shared style FEATURES fill:#f7fcf9,stroke:#b5d8c1,color:#17543a style PRODUCTS fill:#f5f9ff,stroke:#b6cbea,color:#17365f style FOUNDATION fill:#fafbfc,stroke:#cbd2dc,color:#334155 ``` **Figure 1: three plugin layers.** Feature plugins build on product plugins, which reuse the core framework and plugins. Group arrows show dependencies on the layer below; Core provides content models, commands, dependency injection, and lifecycle management. Some plugins and dependencies are omitted. New features keep their rules in their own plugins and cooperate through public services, commands, and defined extension points. UI plugins build on shared UI services and components. Dependencies are explicit at two levels: - **Between plugins:** `DependentOn` declares runtime plugin dependencies. The plugin service orders them, and lifecycle stages separate dependency registration, content initialization, and UI initialization. - **Inside plugins:** dependency injection connects controllers and services through declared dependencies. Supported overrides let an application replace an implementation, adapt a platform service, or supply a test double. Instance-scoped injectors keep application state separate between Univer instances. Disposable registration also gives commands, listeners, components, and icons a cleanup path when their owner is disposed. The [filter plugin](./packages/sheets-filter/src/plugin.ts) and its [UI plugin](./packages/sheets-filter-ui/src/plugin.ts) show these boundaries in working code.
Inside a feature: Model, Controller, Service, and the UI foundation For filtering, `sheets-filter` owns content logic and `sheets-filter-ui` owns UI interaction. Each module has a focused responsibility. ```mermaid %%{init: {'htmlLabels': false, 'theme': 'base', 'themeVariables': {'fontFamily': 'Arial, PingFang SC, Microsoft YaHei, sans-serif', 'fontSize': '17px', 'lineColor': '#64748b'}, 'flowchart': {'htmlLabels': false, 'curve': 'linear', 'nodeSpacing': 28, 'rankSpacing': 45, 'padding': 16, 'wrappingWidth': 270}}}%% %% Every arrow means contains. This is code organization, not execution order. flowchart LR FEATURE["Filter Feature"] LOGIC["Filter Plugin"] UI["Filter UI Plugin"] MODEL["Model"] SERVICE["Service"] CONTROLLER["Controller"] COMMAND["Command / Mutation"] FACADE["Facade API"] VIEW["View"] UICTRL["UI Controller"] UISERVICE["UI Service"] FEATURE --> LOGIC FEATURE --> UI LOGIC --> MODEL LOGIC --> SERVICE LOGIC --> CONTROLLER LOGIC --> COMMAND LOGIC --> FACADE UI --> VIEW UI --> UICTRL UI --> UISERVICE classDef logic fill:#eff6ff,color:#17365f,stroke:#93b4df,stroke-width:1.5px classDef ui fill:#f0fdf4,color:#17543a,stroke:#91c8a7,stroke-width:1.5px classDef shared fill:#f6f7f9,color:#334155,stroke:#bac3ce,stroke-width:1.5px classDef feature fill:#172d50,color:#ffffff,stroke:#172d50 class FEATURE feature class LOGIC,MODEL,SERVICE,CONTROLLER,COMMAND,FACADE logic class UI,VIEW,UICTRL,UISERVICE ui ``` **Figure 2: code organization. Arrows mean “contains.”** Both plugins can contain Controllers and Services: logic Controllers coordinate content changes and related features; UI Controllers connect menus, shortcuts, and interactions, with UI Services managing panel state. These responsibilities give new features a consistent structure to implement and test. The UI foundation follows the same division. **`@univerjs/design`** supplies shared components and styles, **`@univerjs/ui`** provides workbench services such as menus, shortcuts, panels, and component registration, and **`@univerjs/icons`** supplies icons. A feature registers its components and icons, contributes menus, and attaches its rendering through these extension points. Teams can add a panel or toolbar feature while reusing the application's UI infrastructure. See the [UI overview](https://docs.univer.ai/guides/sheets/ui/overview) and the filter plugin's [component and icon registration](./packages/sheets-filter-ui/src/controllers/components.controller.ts).
### Compose cross-feature edits and undo/redo For example, when rows are inserted inside a filter range, the filter plugin supplies the corresponding range change and its undo data. The row command composes the base edit and participating feature changes, executes them, and records their undo/redo information together. The row insertion feature can use the shared extension mechanism while the filter plugin owns its range-update rules. The command system distinguishes three kinds of action: - **Command** orchestrates a business action and the changes it requires. - **Mutation** changes content saved in a snapshot, with serializable parameters. - **Operation** changes transient state, such as an open panel or the scroll position. **A shared structure for undo/redo.** For an undoable edit, the feature implementation supplies the forward mutations and corresponding inverse mutations, and the Command records them through `IUndoRedoService`. When one action affects several features, the Command can combine their changes and undo data in a single undo/redo record, so the user can undo and redo the complete action. See [extending commands](https://docs.univer.ai/blog/custom-command). Features still need to cooperate. **Interceptors and reference-range handlers give that cooperation a defined place.** At supported extension points, plugins contribute checks or related mutations; interceptor priorities control ordering where the API defines it.
Example: commands, callbacks, feature coordination, and undo/redo ```mermaid %%{init: {'htmlLabels': false, 'theme': 'base', 'themeVariables': {'fontFamily': 'Arial, PingFang SC, Microsoft YaHei, sans-serif', 'fontSize': '17px', 'lineColor': '#64748b'}, 'flowchart': {'htmlLabels': false, 'curve': 'linear', 'nodeSpacing': 28, 'rankSpacing': 45, 'padding': 16, 'wrappingWidth': 270}}}%% %% Simplified insert-row example. A command composes mutations and records undo after success. %% Events may also fire for nested command executions; not every callback is drawn. flowchart TD BEFORE["Before execution
Inspect or cancel"] CMD["Insert-row Command"] BASE["Row mutations"] EXT["Feature extension points
Filter range changes"] MODEL["Execute combined mutations"] UNDO["Record undo and redo"] AFTER["After execution
Notify listeners"] BEFORE --> CMD CMD --> BASE CMD --> EXT BASE --> MODEL EXT --> MODEL MODEL --> UNDO UNDO --> AFTER classDef entry fill:#f6f7f9,color:#334155,stroke:#bac3ce,stroke-width:1.5px classDef core fill:#eff6ff,color:#17365f,stroke:#93b4df,stroke-width:1.5px classDef extension fill:#f0fdf4,color:#17543a,stroke:#91c8a7,stroke-width:1.5px class BEFORE,AFTER entry class CMD,BASE,MODEL,UNDO core class EXT extension ``` This diagram simplifies an insert-row workflow. Nested command executions have their own callbacks; it does not show every event or the separate Operation path. See the [row command](./packages/sheets/src/commands/commands/insert-row-col.command.ts), [filter controller](./packages/sheets-filter/src/controllers/sheets-filter.controller.ts), and [interceptor service](./packages/sheets/src/services/sheet-interceptor/sheet-interceptor.service.ts).
These boundaries support a practical testing strategy: test models and services independently, replace external dependencies through DI, and add regression cases for combined actions and undo/redo. The [filter controller tests](./packages/sheets-filter/src/controllers/__tests__/sheets-filter.controller.spec.ts) exercise row and column changes and their effect on filtering. ### Connect applications and agents through Facade APIs and events The repository includes the content models, formula engine, and Canvas rendering and layout engine behind the editors. They are shared building blocks: spreadsheet rich text, for example, reuses document layout and rendering. Custom features can build on these engines instead of implementing a separate content stack. Read about the [formula engine architecture](https://docs.univer.ai/blog/formula) and [rendering engine architecture](https://docs.univer.ai/blog/rendering). Browser editors, Node.js Headless tasks, and appropriately composed Workers can reuse the corresponding content plugins, models, commands, and calculation. See [Headless Univer](https://docs.univer.ai/guides/sheets/getting-started/node) and the [isomorphic architecture](./docs/ISOMORPHIC.md). `ICommandService` exposes execution callbacks so plugins can observe commands before and after execution. Facade APIs wrap the underlying capabilities in application objects such as `FWorkbook`, `FWorksheet`, and `FRange`. Each plugin contributes its own Facade extensions, **typed events through `univerAPI.Event`**, and **enums through `univerAPI.Enum`**. Application code can discover event names and constants from one entry point instead of importing private services or repeating strings. For example, `BeforeCommandExecute` can inspect and cancel an execution; `CommandExecuted` reports executions to listeners. Listeners return disposables, and cancellation applies where the event supports it. Facade extensions stay with their feature packages, so a content API does not have to pull in unrelated UI APIs. See the [Facade design](https://docs.univer.ai/blog/facade), [command callbacks and event bridge](./packages/core/src/facade/f-univer.ts), and [Enum entry point](./packages/core/src/facade/f-enum.ts). The repository provides working feature implementations and patterns for extending them. Read the [filter implementation walkthrough](https://docs.univer.ai/blog/anatomy) for a complete example, or the [API Stability Policy](./docs/API_STABILITY.md) before depending on an extension point.

## 🧩 Extend your application with Univer Office SDK

When you want more ready-to-integrate capabilities, compose the corresponding **Univer Office SDK** modules: additional content types, advanced editing plugins, collaboration, file conversion, and agent tooling. They extend the same content models, plugin architecture, command system, and Facade design introduced above, so you can build on your existing integration.
Part How it extends the foundation
Open-source Web SDK core · this repository Open-source models, engines, plugins, UI foundation, and Sheets and Docs capabilities, with corresponding Headless content operations. Use them in commercial applications under Apache-2.0.
Commercial Web SDK plugins Follow the core's Plugin, dependency injection, Command/Mutation, and Facade extension patterns. Add charts, shapes, pivot tables, SmartArt, and other features for the corresponding content types.
Server SDK Extends the same content models and mutation conventions with real-time collaboration, revision history, and Office file conversion. Integrates with your application's identity, permissions, and storage.
AI SDK extensions Reuse Web SDK Headless and Facade capabilities to provide composable Node.js APIs and CLI building blocks for agents to inspect, edit, and check content, with collaboration and Worktree review integrations.
### Scope and licensing - **This repository:** Apache-2.0 packages that can be used in commercial applications under that license, including the open-source Headless content capabilities. - **Commercial extensions:** Commercial Web SDK plugins, Server SDK, and AI SDK capabilities beyond the open-source foundation are distributed and licensed separately. **Freemium** evaluation includes watermarks and feature limits. - **Reference applications:** Open-source applications such as Univer Workspace have their own source licenses. Their SDK dependencies retain their respective licenses. See the [feature comparison](https://univer.ai/compare/), including its **Open source only** filter, for detailed coverage and [plans and licensing](https://univer.ai/pricing/) for commercial options.
How shared content models connect editing, collaboration, and files These capabilities operate on serializable **Unit snapshots**, including Sheets' `IWorkbookData`, Docs' `IDocumentData`, Slides' `ISlideData`, and canvases' `IBoardData` (called **Boards** in the API). These types come from core and the respective product packages; current Slides and Boards capabilities are separately distributed commercial products. The shared Unit conventions let browser editors, backend services, and agents work with the same content. Commands orchestrate edits; **Mutations describe content changes**. Collaboration packages those mutations into **changesets**, applies **operational transformation (OT)** to concurrent changes, and manages confirmed revisions and snapshots. History can reconstruct a revision from a snapshot and subsequent changesets. Read the [collaboration design](https://docs.univer.ai/blog/ot) and [Collaboration SDK overview](https://docs.univer.ai/server/collaboration/overview). **Exchange** maps Office file structures to and from Univer content snapshots. For OOXML formats such as **XLSX, DOCX, and PPTX**, it parses the file into the corresponding Sheet, Doc, or Slide data and generates the file representation on export. The converted content can enter the same editing, calculation, collaboration, and agent workflows. See [Office file import and export](https://docs.univer.ai/server/import-export/node).
How AI SDK gives agents the same content capabilities AI SDK builds on the Web SDK's **Headless content models, commands, calculation, and Facade APIs**. It exposes structured TypeScript APIs and optional Commander presets that applications can compose into their own Office CLI or agent tools. - **Understand, discover, and edit.** Inspection returns structured content. API Reference helps the agent find Facade symbols and signatures shipped with its SDK. Facade execution distinguishes read and write modes, captures mutations, and works with explicit synchronization and commit results. See [content operations](https://docs.univer.ai/ai/content-operations). - **Check the rendered result.** A browser Render Runtime reuses Web SDK rendering for screenshots. Slide layout lint adds structured findings for issues such as off-page or overlapping text, giving the agent evidence for another editing pass. See [visual inspection](https://docs.univer.ai/ai/visual-inspection). - **Edit drafts for human review.** With the corresponding collaboration and Web capabilities, agents can edit and verify an isolated Worktree draft over several rounds, then hand it to a person to review, merge, or reopen. The workflow uses the same snapshots, mutations, and revision conventions. See [Worktree](https://docs.univer.ai/ai/worktree). For repeated calls, optional [Worker pools and a daemon](https://docs.univer.ai/ai/runtime-architecture) reuse loaded content instances and reduce repeated initialization. Your application owns the root CLI, targets, authorization, and output. Explore the [AI SDK package catalog](https://docs.univer.ai/ai/packages) to select the required capabilities.

## 🌐 Application patterns and ecosystem

### Univer Workspace: an Office SDK reference application For a complete application reference, start with [Univer Workspace](https://github.com/dream-num/univer-workspace). It shows how to compose Univer Office SDK editors, collaboration, file capabilities, existing agents, and human review into a self-hostable workspace. Follow its integration patterns when building your own Office application or agent workspace.

[Watch an SDK integration demo](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=1p-SMEiK6Kg) ### CLI, agent integrations, and developer skills The same SDK capabilities can also be composed into the agents and tools you already use:

Each repository documents its setup and SDK dependencies. Explore the [ecosystem](https://univer.ai/ecosystem/) for agent entry points, or the [documentation](https://docs.univer.ai/) to build your own integration.

Univer is compiled with a Chrome 88 target and aims to work with the versions listed above.

### Runtime compatibility - **Polyfills**: Univer relies on `Intl.Segmenter`. Add a polyfill such as `@formatjs/intl-segmenter` if your target browser or runtime does not provide it. - **Build tools**: We recommend Vite, esbuild, or Webpack 5. If your build tool does not support the `exports` field in `package.json` (common in Webpack 4), you may need extra path mapping. - **React**: Univer's view layer is built on React 18, supports React 18 and 19, and provides minimal compatibility support for React 16.9+ and 17. - **Node.js runtime**: Headless Univer supports Node.js `>=18.17.0`. Developing this monorepo requires Node.js `>=22.18`.
Developing in this repository ### Repository layout ```text . ├── packages/ Core packages, engines, document types, UI plugins, and feature plugins ├── examples/ All-in-one Vite workbench used for local browser development ├── common/ Shared internal tooling, storybook, and utilities ├── tests/ Additional integration test projects └── docs/ Architecture notes, images, and repository-local documentation ``` Package-level READMEs live beside each package under [`packages/`](./packages). ### Local development Requirements: - Node.js `>=22.18` - pnpm: use the version declared by `packageManager` in `package.json`. ```bash git clone https://github.com/dream-num/univer.git cd univer pnpm install pnpm dev ``` Useful commands:

repositories.readme:
# Faiss

Faiss is a library for efficient similarity search and clustering of dense vectors. It contains algorithms that search in sets of vectors of any size, up to ones that possibly do not fit in RAM. It also contains supporting code for evaluation and parameter tuning. Faiss is written in C++ with complete wrappers for Python/numpy. Some of the most useful algorithms are implemented on the GPU. It is developed primarily at Meta's [Fundamental AI Research](https://ai.facebook.com/) group.

## News

See [CHANGELOG.md](CHANGELOG.md) for detailed information about latest features.

## Introduction

Faiss contains several methods for similarity search. It assumes that the instances are represented as vectors and are identified by an integer, and that the vectors can be compared with L2 (Euclidean) distances or dot products. Vectors that are similar to a query vector are those that have the lowest L2 distance or the highest dot product with the query vector. It also supports cosine similarity, since this is a dot product on normalized vectors.

Some of the methods, like those based on binary vectors and compact quantization codes, solely use a compressed representation of the vectors and do not require to keep the original vectors. This generally comes at the cost of a less precise search but these methods can scale to billions of vectors in main memory on a single server. Other methods, like HNSW and NSG add an indexing structure on top of the raw vectors to make searching more efficient.

The GPU implementation can accept input from either CPU or GPU memory. On a server with GPUs, the GPU indexes can be used a drop-in replacement for the CPU indexes (e.g., replace `IndexFlatL2` with `GpuIndexFlatL2`) and copies to/from GPU memory are handled automatically. Results will be faster however if both input and output remain resident on the GPU. Both single and multi-GPU usage is supported.

## Installing

Faiss comes with precompiled libraries for Anaconda in Python, see [faiss-cpu](https://anaconda.org/pytorch/faiss-cpu), [faiss-gpu](https://anaconda.org/pytorch/faiss-gpu) and [faiss-gpu-cuvs](https://anaconda.org/pytorch/faiss-gpu-cuvs). The library is mostly implemented in C++, the only dependency is a [BLAS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Basic_Linear_Algebra_Subprograms) implementation. Optional GPU support is provided via CUDA or AMD ROCm, and the Python interface is also optional. The backend GPU implementations of NVIDIA [cuVS](https://github.com/rapidsai/cuvs) can also be enabled optionally. It compiles with cmake. See [INSTALL.md](INSTALL.md) for details.

## How Faiss works

Faiss is built around an index type that stores a set of vectors, and provides a function to search in them with L2 and/or dot product vector comparison. Some index types are simple baselines, such as exact search. Most of the available indexing structures correspond to various trade-offs with respect to

- search time
- search quality
- memory used per index vector
- training time
- adding time
- need for external data for unsupervised training

The optional GPU implementation provides what is likely (as of March 2017) the fastest exact and approximate (compressed-domain) nearest neighbor search implementation for high-dimensional vectors, fastest Lloyd's k-means, and fastest small k-selection algorithm known. [The implementation is detailed here](https://arxiv.org/abs/1702.08734).

## Full documentation of Faiss

The following are entry points for documentation:

- the full documentation can be found on the [wiki page](https://github.com/facebookresearch/faiss/wiki), including a [tutorial](https://github.com/facebookresearch/faiss/wiki/Getting-started), a [FAQ](https://github.com/facebookresearch/faiss/wiki/FAQ) and a [troubleshooting section](https://github.com/facebookresearch/faiss/wiki/Troubleshooting)
- the [doxygen documentation](https://faiss.ai/) gives per-class information extracted from code comments
- to reproduce results from our research papers, [Polysemous codes](https://arxiv.org/abs/1609.01882) and [Billion-scale similarity search with GPUs](https://arxiv.org/abs/1702.08734), refer to the [benchmarks README](benchs/README.md). For [
Link and code: Fast indexing with graphs and compact regression codes](https://arxiv.org/abs/1804.09996), see the [link_and_code README](benchs/link_and_code)

## Authors

The main authors of Faiss are:
- [Hervé Jégou](https://github.com/jegou) initiated the Faiss project and wrote its first implementation
- [Matthijs Douze](https://github.com/mdouze) implemented most of the CPU Faiss
- [Jeff Johnson](https://github.com/wickedfoo) implemented all of the GPU Faiss
- [Lucas Hosseini](https://github.com/beauby) implemented the binary indexes and the build system
- [Chengqi Deng](https://github.com/KinglittleQ) implemented NSG, NNdescent and much of the additive quantization code.
- [Alexandr Guzhva](https://github.com/alexanderguzhva) many optimizations: SIMD, memory allocation and layout, fast decoding kernels for vector codecs, etc.
- [Gergely Szilvasy](https://github.com/algoriddle) build system, benchmarking framework.

You can report bugs, ask questions, etc.

repositories.description: Open-source LLM knowledge platform: turn raw documents into a queryable RAG, an autonomous reasoning agent, and a self-maintaining Wiki.
repositories.readme:
English · 简体中文 · 日本語 · 한국어

Overview · Quick Start · What's New · Features · Clients · Docs · Development

## Overview [WeKnora](https://weknora.weixin.qq.com) is an open-source, LLM-powered knowledge framework for enterprise document understanding, semantic retrieval and reasoning. It brings a team's documents together so they can be searched, reasoned over and kept up to date. https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/de0e490a-e738-405e-bb3a-64b63edd7278

v0.9.0 · 2:45 · 1080p60 · English narration and subtitles

Use RAG to look things up, the agent for multi-step tasks, and the wiki to organize knowledge. All three work on the same knowledge bases. **The agent's toolbox.** Skills installed from ClawHub / SkillHub / Git / ZIP run in session-persistent Docker / E2B / Cube sandboxes, with an interactive terminal and graphical desktop beside the chat. Through the BrowserSkill extension the agent operates the user's own Chrome or Edge, and external MCP services (OAuth included) can be connected and enabled tool by tool. Beyond the three modes: - **Memory and curation**: cross-session long-term memory keeps the profile, preferences and facts a user has confirmed. Folder uploads keep their directory tree, and retrieval chunks can be edited, diffed and rolled back. - **Data sources and formats**: auto-sync from Feishu wiki / Feishu Drive / Confluence / GitLab / Tencent IMA / Notion / Yuque / DingTalk Docs / Seafile / RSS, with more on the way. 10+ document formats including PDF, Word, images, Excel and XMind; Office files are parsed in-process by anydoc. - **Channels and integrations**: Q&A in WeCom, Feishu, Slack, Telegram and other IM apps; an embed widget for external websites; a built-in MCP Server for Cursor, Claude and other AI tools; scoped API keys with a principal model for programmatic access. - **Models**: 29 built-in vendors with a generated model catalog, including OpenAI, DeepSeek, Qwen (Alibaba Cloud), Zhipu, Hunyuan, Gemini, MiniMax, NVIDIA, LiteLLM and Ollama. - **Permissions and operations**: multi-workspace RBAC (four roles, per-resource ownership, per-workspace audit log), several storage instances per workspace, a runtime task-queue dashboard with worker-pool governance, and Langfuse tracing for agent steps, token usage and pipelines. - **Deployment**: LLMs, vector databases and storage backends are all swappable. Deploy locally or on a private cloud and keep the data in your own environment. ## Quick Start

ONLINE
WeChat Dialog Open Platform
Manage knowledge bases online and connect Q&A to Official Accounts, Mini Programs and other WeChat scenarios.

Open the platform →
CLOUD
Tencent Cloud Lighthouse
Deploy WeKnora from an application template and run it on your own cloud server.

Deploy on Tencent Cloud →
SELF-HOSTED
Your own environment
Deploy with Docker or Kubernetes and configure models, storage and networking yourself.

Run with Docker Compose ↓
### Run with Docker Compose Requires [Docker](https://www.docker.com/), [Docker Compose](https://docs.docker.com/compose/) and [Git](https://git-scm.com/). ```bash git clone https://github.com/Tencent/WeKnora.git cd WeKnora cp .env.example .env # Edit .env as needed, see comments in the file docker compose pull # Pull the latest images docker compose up -d # Start core services ``` Then open **http://localhost** and follow the onboarding guide. A walkthrough with sample data is in the [Quickstart](https://weknora.weixin.qq.com/docs/01-getting-started/03-quickstart). > [!TIP] > To use a local Ollama model, run `ollama serve > /dev/null 2>&1 &` first. For the Ollama embedding model name, `OLLAMA_BASE_URL`, and RAM notes, see [Configuration](https://weknora.weixin.qq.com/docs/01-getting-started/04-configuration). | Service | URL | |---------|-----| | Web UI | `http://localhost` | | Backend API | `http://localhost:8080` | | Langfuse Tracing | `http://localhost:3000` | ### Optional services Add `--profile` flags to enable additional components; multiple profiles can be combined. | Profile | Adds | |---------|------| | _(default)_ | Core services | | `full` | All features | | `neo4j` | Knowledge Graph (Neo4j) | | `minio` | Object Storage (MinIO) | | `langfuse` | Tracing (Langfuse) | ```bash docker compose --profile neo4j --profile minio pull docker compose --profile neo4j --profile minio up -d docker compose down # Stop services ``` ### Upgrading If you already have WeKnora running and downloaded a newer release: ```bash # Set WEKNORA_VERSION in .env to the target release (e.g. 0.9.0), or keep latest docker compose pull # Pull images matching WEKNORA_VERSION docker compose up -d # Recreate containers with new images ``` > [!NOTE] > `docker compose up -d` alone reuses locally cached images and may leave the UI version out of sync with the release you downloaded. Read the [upgrade notes](https://weknora.weixin.qq.com/docs/07-releases/v0.9.0#upgrade-notes) before upgrading. Deployments older than v0.8.2 should also read the [v0.8.2 notes](https://weknora.weixin.qq.com/docs/07-releases/v0.8.2#upgrade-notes). ### Other ways to deploy | Option | When to use it | |--------|----------------| | **Docker Compose** | The standard deployment above: all features, multiple services | | **Kubernetes (Helm)** | Production clusters; the chart is in [`helm/`](./helm) | | **Lite single binary** | Local or low-resource use with no external dependencies (SQLite + in-memory queue); see [Lite vs. standard](./docs/LITE.md) | | **Desktop app** | The Lite runtime with a GUI, login-free start and a macOS host sandbox; no installer is published yet, so build it from source | All options, hardware requirements and deployment topologies: [Installation guide](https://weknora.weixin.qq.com/docs/01-getting-started/02-installation). > [!WARNING] > WeKnora ships with login authentication, but for production deployments we strongly recommend that you: > - deploy it in an internal / private network rather than on the public internet; > - avoid exposing the service directly to public networks, to prevent information leakage; > - configure proper firewall rules and access controls for the deployment environment; > - regularly update to the latest version for security patches and improvements. ## What's New ### v0.9.0 · 2026-10-29 · [release notes](https://weknora.weixin.qq.com/docs/07-releases/v0.9.0) - **[WeKnora assistant](https://weknora.weixin.qq.com/docs/07-releases/v0.9.0#assistant)**: Ask about WeKnora releases, features and configuration, then work from the current page: create agents, schedule tasks and manage knowledge, acting as you within your permissions. - **[Multi-agent collaboration](https://weknora.weixin.qq.com/docs/07-releases/v0.9.0#collaboration)**: Delegate independent subtasks, follow progress and bring the results together. - **[Automations](https://weknora.weixin.qq.com/docs/07-releases/v0.9.0#automations)**: Run one-off or recurring tasks with execution history, results and approval notifications. - **[Execution permissions](https://weknora.weixin.qq.com/docs/07-releases/v0.9.0#permissions)**: Read-only, confirm-before-change and automatic-write modes, with scoped session and automation grants. - **[Sandboxes and background work](https://weknora.weixin.qq.com/docs/07-releases/v0.9.0#sandbox)**: Optional per-user sandbox reuse, managed background shell jobs and skill rollout controls. - **[Parsing, sync and retrieval](https://weknora.weixin.qq.com/docs/07-releases/v0.9.0#knowledge)**: Configurable image pipelines, OCR preprocessing, deeper Feishu/Lark sync, Confluence PAT and retrieval improvements. - **[Upgrade notes](https://weknora.weixin.qq.com/docs/07-releases/v0.9.0#upgrade-notes)**: Review database migrations, Feishu resync, the sandbox allocation gate and configuration changes. ### v0.8.3 · 2026-10-14 · [release notes](https://weknora.weixin.qq.com/docs/07-releases/v0.8.3) - **[Image gallery](https://weknora.weixin.qq.com/docs/07-releases/v0.8.3#images)**: browse document images and filter by source, caption, OCR and image attributes. - **[Multimodal Embedding](https://weknora.weixin.qq.com/docs/07-releases/v0.8.3#multimodal-embedding)**: support for multimodal embedding models that encode text and images into a shared vector space, including Tencent WeMM-Embedding and Qwen3-VL-Embedding, with opt-in image-vector retrieval and compatible image-aware reranking. - **[Wiki graph](https://weknora.weixin.qq.com/docs/07-releases/v0.8.3#wiki-graph)**: clearer group layouts and theme captions, with group focus, switching and return to the full graph. - **[Source citations](https://weknora.weixin.qq.com/docs/07-releases/v0.8.3#conversation)**: navigate from an answer to the cited passage in the original document. - **[Chat and tools](https://weknora.weixin.qq.com/docs/07-releases/v0.8.3#tools)**: on-demand attachment reading without a sandbox, unread replies, @ mention search, Docker terminals, Lite host skills and MCP interoperability updates. - **[Administration and integrations](https://weknora.weixin.qq.com/docs/07-releases/v0.8.3#administration)**: platform user management, invitation-only signup mode, administrator model catalog, WeMM embeddings, TEI/Pinecone/Cohere reranking, Seafile and Traditional Chinese. - **[Reliability](https://weknora.weixin.qq.com/docs/07-releases/v0.8.3#other-changes)**: broad retrieval, parsing, datasource, Wiki, OAuth and CLI fixes. Review [upgrade requirements](https://weknora.weixin.qq.com/docs/07-releases/v0.8.3#upgrade-notes) for registration modes, empty tool lists, database migrations and reindexing. ### v0.8.2 · 2026-09-24 · [release notes](https://weknora.weixin.qq.com/docs/07-releases/v0.8.2) Agents can operate the browser on your computer, knowledge bases can be published to other AI tools over MCP, and a running conversation can be steered, forked or rewound. - **[Local Browser (BrowserSkill)](https://weknora.weixin.qq.com/docs/07-releases/v0.8.2#local-browser)**: agents drive the user's own Chrome / Edge through the open-source BrowserSkill extension, with a live task preview, pause / resume and hand-off for logins and CAPTCHAs. - **[Built-in MCP Server](https://weknora.weixin.qq.com/docs/07-releases/v0.8.2#mcp-server)**: per-workspace `/mcp/` endpoints over Streamable HTTP, each with its own token, knowledge-base scope, rate limit and tool groups. The Python `mcp-server/` is deprecated. - **[Conversation control](https://weknora.weixin.qq.com/docs/07-releases/v0.8.2#conversation-control)**: append requirements to a running turn, fork from any earlier question, rewind in place with sandbox checkpoints, and pick reasoning effort per session. Generated files are collected in a new artifacts library. - **[Sandbox](https://weknora.weixin.qq.com/docs/07-releases/v0.8.2#sandbox)**: interactive terminal and graphical desktop; macOS Lite host sandbox with project folders; a sidebar Toolbox for skills, MCP services and the browser connection. - **[Models](https://weknora.weixin.qq.com/docs/07-releases/v0.8.2#models)**: rebuilt model catalog (27 built-in vendors with generated context-window, max-output, reasoning and vision metadata). Agent retrieval tools are consolidated into `search_knowledge` / `read_document` / `list_documents`. - **[Knowledge and platform](https://weknora.weixin.qq.com/docs/07-releases/v0.8.2#knowledge)**: Confluence and DingTalk Docs data sources; Bocha and Serply web search; Japanese UI; per-channel IM reply language; whitelist-only outbound mode. > [!IMPORTANT] > **Breaking:** DingTalk channels are Stream-only, and sandbox commands run as `root`. See the [upgrade notes](https://weknora.weixin.qq.com/docs/07-releases/v0.8.2#upgrade-notes). ### v0.8.0 · [release notes](https://weknora.weixin.qq.com/docs/07-releases/v0.8.0) - **Skill sandbox runtime**: session-persistent Docker / E2B / Cube backends with per-tenant network policy; the Local host-process backend is removed and Docker is opt-in. - **Tenant skill catalog**: install from ClawHub / SkillHub / git / zip, with per-sandbox snapshots, live progress, file browse/edit, and personal and workspace env vars. - **Cross-session long-term memory**: profile / preference / fact / task / interest, auto-extracted with user confirmation, plus `search_memory`. - **Parsing and sources**: in-process anydoc office parser; GitLab and Tencent IMA data sources; XMind parsing. - **Ecosystem**: official DeepSeek Harness plugin `@wxg-prc-cpg/dsh-weknora`; LiteLLM; Exa and Metaso web search. - **Chat**: chat artifacts, question outline and timestamps; context compaction and provider prompt-cache markers. - **Security**: OIDC JWKS verification, optional complex passwords, document auto-tagging, and broad sandbox/security hardening.
Earlier releases (v0.2.0 – v0.7.2)
- **v0.7.2** — Product documentation site; knowledge base folder tree; chunk editing with revision history; wiki page revisions; directly loadable file URLs (`resource_urls=public`); Feishu Drive data source; batch tagging; MCP Server 1.1 (29 tools); AWS S3 default credential chain. - **v0.7.1** — Yunzhijia IM; Volcengine rerank; Zhipu AI web search; platform-scoped API keys; per-KB activity audit; FAQ filtering, tagging and export; Langfuse OTLP tracing; one-click Markdown export. - **v0.7.0** — Scoped API keys and principal model; task-queue dashboard and worker-pool governance; multiple storage instances per workspace; temporary chat attachments; `@Skill / @MCP` mentions; mid-conversation MCP OAuth; QQBot and Lark IM; Redis TLS; `weknora` CLI v0.10. - **v0.6.3** — Website embed widget & Integrations Center (secure-mode token exchange + rate limits); OpenDataLoader + PaddleOCR-VL parsers; MCP server multi-transport (stdio / SSE / HTTP); per-model thinking-mode config; Tencent LKEAP rerank + native Gemini embeddings + MiniMax-M3. - **v0.6.0** — Workspace RBAC (4-tier role matrix `Owner` / `Admin` / `Contributor` / `Viewer` + per-KB ownership + per-workspace audit log), workspace member management & multi-workspace UX, self-service workspaces; `weknora` CLI v0.4 GA with `mcp serve`; KB retrieval fan-out across vector stores; AES-256-GCM credential encryption + docreader gRPC TLS + Token; Zhipu embedder + Huawei OBS; server-side user preferences; Go 1.26.0. See [Tenants & auth](https://weknora.weixin.qq.com/docs/03-features/01-tenant-auth). - **v0.5.2** — Wiki ingest scales to 40k-document KBs (task queue + DLQ); MCP human-in-the-loop tool approval; Anthropic / Apache Doris / Tencent VectorDB / KS3 / SearXNG backends; adaptive 3-tier chunking with live preview; global ⌘K command palette; Yuque connector + WeChat Mini Program; `weknora` CLI preview. - **v0.5.1** — Knowledge-base batch management; workspace-wide IM channels overview; wiki browser + visual graph in the UI. - **v0.4.0** — WeKnora Cloud (hosted LLM + parsing); Chrome Extension; ClawHub Skill; WeChat IM; attachment processing; Azure OpenAI / Alibaba OSS; Notion connector; Baidu + Ollama web search; VectorStore management. - **v0.3.6** — ASR (audio); Feishu data-source auto-sync; OIDC; IM quote-reply context + thread-based sessions; document summarization; Tavily search; parallel tool calling; agent @mention scope restriction. - **v0.3.5** — Telegram / DingTalk / Mattermost IM; IM slash commands + QA queue; suggested questions; VLM auto-describe MCP tool images; Novita AI; `final_answer` tool. - **v0.3.3** — Parent-child chunking; KB pinning; fallback response; passage cleaning for rerank; storage auto-creation; Milvus. - **v0.3.2** — Knowledge Search entry; per-source parser & storage engine config;
