custom agents; Data Analyst agent; thinking mode; Bing / Google web search; API Key auth; Helm chart; Korean i18n; Qdrant. - **v0.2.0** — Agent Mode (ReACT); multi-type knowledge bases (FAQ + document); conversation strategy config; DuckDuckGo web search; MCP tool integration; new UI with agent mode switching; MQ async task management. Full history: [`CHANGELOG.md`](./CHANGELOG.md).
## Product Tour ### Quick Q&A and smart reasoning **Two ways to ask.** Quick Q&A answers from the knowledge base with RAG and cites the sources it used. In smart reasoning the agent plans multi-step work, searching, reading documents and calling tools and skills, and shows each step in the conversation. [Docs →](https://weknora.weixin.qq.com/docs/03-features/18-chat-experience) ### Local browser **Operate the browser on your computer.** Through Tencent's open-source BrowserSkill extension, the agent opens pages and fills in forms in your own Chrome or Edge, and hands over to you for logins and CAPTCHAs. [Docs →](https://weknora.weixin.qq.com/docs/05-clients/09-local-browser) ### Skills and sandbox **Run skills and produce files.** Docker, E2B and Cube backends are supported. Turns in the same session share one workspace, and generated files can be previewed and downloaded. Open the graphical desktop or interactive terminal beside the chat to follow each step and take over when needed. [Docs →](https://weknora.weixin.qq.com/docs/03-features/22-skills-sandbox) ### Toolbox: MCP services and skills **Tools the agent can use.** Connect external MCP services and choose, tool by tool, which are enabled and which calls need approval. Install skills from ClawHub, SkillHub, Git or ZIP, manage them per workspace, and reuse them across sandboxes. [Docs →](https://weknora.weixin.qq.com/docs/03-features/22-skills-sandbox) ### Automatic wiki **Documents organized into a browsable wiki.** With Wiki enabled, WeKnora extracts people, products and concepts from knowledge-base documents into pages with source citations, organized by directory. The knowledge graph shows how pages relate; pages can be edited directly and every change can be rolled back. [Docs →](https://weknora.weixin.qq.com/docs/03-features/14-wiki) ### Observability **Tracing and runtime monitoring.** Langfuse traces the reasoning, tool calls and token usage of each agent step. The document parsing timeline shows progress stage by stage, and the task-queue dashboard lists queued and failed tasks. [Docs →](https://weknora.weixin.qq.com/docs/03-features/16-observability) ## Architecture A modular pipeline from document parsing, vectorization and retrieval to LLM inference, in which every component can be replaced or extended. It runs locally or on a private cloud, and the Web UI needs no setup to get started. More: [Architecture overview](https://weknora.weixin.qq.com/docs/02-architecture/01-overview) · [RAG pipeline](https://weknora.weixin.qq.com/docs/02-architecture/04-rag-pipeline) · [Extension points](https://weknora.weixin.qq.com/docs/06-development/03-extension-points). ## Features | Area | Highlights | |------|------------| | [Q&A and agent](https://weknora.weixin.qq.com/docs/03-features/07-agent) | Quick Q&A answers from knowledge bases with citations; smart reasoning runs a ReAct agent over knowledge bases, web search, MCP tools, skills and the local browser. Steer, fork or rewind a running conversation, and keep [long-term memory](https://weknora.weixin.qq.com/docs/03-features/23-memory) across sessions | | [Wiki](https://weknora.weixin.qq.com/docs/03-features/14-wiki) | Agent-generated, interlinked wiki pages with a knowledge graph; in-browser editing, revision diff and rollback | | [Skills and sandbox](https://weknora.weixin.qq.com/docs/03-features/22-skills-sandbox) | Skill catalog installed from ClawHub / SkillHub / Git / ZIP; session-persistent Docker / E2B / Cube sandboxes with network policy; terminal and graphical desktop beside the chat | | [Knowledge bases](https://weknora.weixin.qq.com/docs/03-features/02-knowledge-base) | FAQ, document and wiki bases; folder tree; chunk editing with revisions; per-upload parsing, chunking and multimodal settings; auto-tagging | | [Retrieval](https://weknora.weixin.qq.com/docs/03-features/05-retrieval-engines) | Keyword + vector hybrid search, rerank, parent-child chunking and GraphRAG ([Neo4j](https://weknora.weixin.qq.com/docs/03-features/09-knowledge-graph)); end-to-end evaluation with recall and BLEU / ROUGE | | [Access and security](https://weknora.weixin.qq.com/docs/03-features/01-tenant-auth) | Workspace RBAC with four roles and an audit log; scoped API keys; OIDC; AES-256-GCM credential encryption; SSRF-safe outbound requests with a whitelist-only mode | | [Operations](https://weknora.weixin.qq.com/docs/03-features/16-observability) | Langfuse tracing for agent steps, tokens and pipelines; document parsing timeline; task-queue dashboard with worker pools; automatic migrations on upgrade | ### Supported backends | Component | Options | |-----------|---------| | [LLMs](https://weknora.weixin.qq.com/docs/03-features/06-models) | 29 built-in vendors, including OpenAI / Azure OpenAI / Anthropic / DeepSeek / Qwen / Zhipu / Hunyuan / Doubao / Gemini / MiniMax / NVIDIA / SiliconFlow / OpenRouter / LiteLLM / Ollama | | Embeddings | Ollama / BGE / GTE / Zhipu / OpenAI-compatible APIs | | Vector databases | PostgreSQL (pgvector + ParadeDB) / Elasticsearch / OpenSearch / Milvus / Weaviate / Qdrant / Apache Doris / Tencent VectorDB | | [Object storage](https://weknora.weixin.qq.com/docs/03-features/19-storage-backends) | Local / Tencent Cloud COS / MinIO / AWS S3 / Volcengine TOS / Alibaba Cloud OSS / Kingsoft Cloud KS3 / Huawei Cloud OBS | | [Document formats](https://weknora.weixin.qq.com/docs/03-features/03-document-parsing) | PDF / Word / PPT / Excel / CSV / TXT / Markdown / HTML / EPUB / MHTML / JSON / XMind / images | | [Data sources](https://weknora.weixin.qq.com/docs/03-features/10-datasource) | Feishu wiki / Feishu Drive / Lark / Confluence / GitLab / Tencent IMA / Notion / Yuque / DingTalk Docs / Seafile / RSS | | [IM channels](https://weknora.weixin.qq.com/docs/03-features/12-im-integration) | WeCom / Feishu / Lark / QQBot / Slack / Telegram / DingTalk / Mattermost / WeChat / Yunzhijia | | [Web search](https://weknora.weixin.qq.com/docs/03-features/11-web-search) | DuckDuckGo / Bing / Google / Tavily / Baidu / Ollama / SearXNG / Keenable / Zhipu AI / Exa / Metaso / Bocha / Serply / SearchApi | | Deployment | Docker Compose / Kubernetes (Helm) / Lite single binary / desktop app; offline and private-cloud installs; UI in Chinese, English, Japanese, Korean and Russian | ## Clients and Integrations | | Client | What it does | |:-:|--------|--------------| | | [**CLI `weknora`**](./cli/README.md) | Agent-first command line for the full API, with a curated MCP tool surface and bundled Agent Skills | | | [**Built-in MCP Server**](https://weknora.weixin.qq.com/docs/03-features/08-mcp) | Publishes knowledge bases to Cursor, Claude and other MCP clients over Streamable HTTP; the Python [`mcp-server/`](./mcp-server/MCP_CONFIG.md) is deprecated | | | [**Local Browser (BrowserSkill)**](https://weknora.weixin.qq.com/docs/05-clients/09-local-browser) | Lets agents operate the user's own Chrome / Edge | | | [**Chrome Extension**](https://chromewebstore.google.com/detail/jpemjbopikggjlmikmclgbmkhhopjdgd) | Select text, images, or entire pages in the browser and save them as knowledge entries with one click, without copy-paste or file upload | | | [**WeChat Mini Program**](./miniprogram/README.md) | Lightweight mobile client: configure API access, select knowledge bases, import URLs, and ask knowledge chat from WeChat | | | [**ClawHub Skill**](https://clawhub.ai/lyingbug/weknora) | A WeKnora skill on ClawHub for document import, hybrid search and knowledge management via the REST API | | | [**DeepSeek Harness plugin**](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@wxg-prc-cpg/dsh-weknora) | Gives `dsh` coding agents four read-only tools: search, read document, ask and list knowledge bases | | | [**Website Embed Widget**](https://weknora.weixin.qq.com/docs/03-features/13-embed-channel) | Publishes agents on external sites | | | [**Go SDK**](https://weknora.weixin.qq.com/docs/05-clients/03-go-sdk) | CRUD for knowledge bases, documents and sessions, plus SSE streaming Q&A | | | [**WeChat Dialog Open Platform**](https://chatbot.weixin.qq.com) | Hosted Q&A built on WeKnora: upload knowledge and publish a Q&A service in WeChat without writing code | ### Command-Line Interface `weknora` is the official CLI for driving the API from a terminal or an AI agent. It is **agent-first**: every command emits a stable JSON envelope by default (with typed error codes mapped to exit codes), and `--format text` renders for humans. It also serves a curated MCP tool surface (`weknora mcp serve`) and ships bundled Agent Skills. ```bash weknora profile add prod --host https://kb.example.com --use weknora auth login weknora kb list weknora link --kb my-knowledge-base # bind the current directory weknora doc upload notes.md weknora chat "summarise the design doc" ``` For headless / CI use, set `WEKNORA_API_KEY` + `WEKNORA_HOST` and skip `auth login`; no credentials are written to disk. See [`cli/README.md`](./cli/README.md) for install + 5-minute quickstart and [`cli/AGENTS.md`](./cli/AGENTS.md) for the operational contract AI agents rely on. ## Documentation The full product documentation lives at **[weknora.weixin.qq.com/docs](https://weknora.weixin.qq.com/docs/)** (in Chinese), organized as Getting Started → Architecture → Features → API → Clients → Development and covering ~360 API endpoints and ~150 environment variables. | Start here | | |------------|---| | [Introduction](https://weknora.weixin.qq.com/docs/01-getting-started/01-introduction) | Capabilities overview | | [Installation](https://weknora.weixin.qq.com/docs/01-getting-started/02-installation) | Docker Compose, Helm, Lite and desktop | | [Configuration](https://weknora.weixin.qq.com/docs/01-getting-started/04-configuration) | Environment variables and models | | [Troubleshooting FAQ](https://weknora.weixin.qq.com/docs/01-getting-started/05-troubleshooting) | Common problems and fixes | | [API reference](https://weknora.weixin.qq.com/docs/04-api/01-api-overview) | REST API overview | | [Release notes](https://weknora.weixin.qq.com/docs/07-releases/v0.9.0) | What changed in each release | ## Development If you need to frequently modify code, you don't need to rebuild Docker images every time. Use fast development mode: ```bash make dev-start # Start infrastructure make dev-app # Start backend (new terminal) make dev-frontend # Start frontend (new terminal) ``` - Frontend modifications auto hot-reload (no restart needed) - Backend modifications quick restart (5-10 seconds, supports Air hot-reload) - No need to rebuild Docker images - Supports IDE breakpoint debugging See the [Development guide](https://weknora.weixin.qq.com/docs/06-development/01-dev-guide) for details. The documentation site and product homepage are built from [`website-docs/`](./website-docs/README.md). With Node.js 24, run `cd website-docs && npm run setup && npm run build && npm run preview` to preview both together; the unified static output serves the homepage at `/` and documentation at `/docs/`. See the directory's README for Nginx and Docker deployment. ## Contributing Welcome to submit [Issues](https://github.com/Tencent/WeKnora/issues) or Pull Requests. - **Process:** Fork → Create branch → Commit changes → Open PR - **Standards:** Format code with `gofmt`, follow [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/) (`feat:` / `fix:` / `docs:` / `test:` / `refactor:`)
Validating your change
For a focused PR, validate the changed scope first: ```bash git fetch origin main git diff --check origin/main...HEAD golangci-lint run --new-from-rev=origin/main ./... go test ./path/to/changed/package -count=1 ``` Run `gofmt` on changed Go files before committing. For frontend changes, run the relevant tests from `frontend/` and use `npm run type-check` when the change affects TypeScript or Vue components. The full maintainer gate remains: ```bash make fmt make lint make test ``` `make fmt` formats the entire Go repository, so run it only with a clean worktree and review the resulting diff. Some full-suite tests require local infrastructure or service configuration. If a full check fails for an unrelated baseline or environment reason, include the exact command and failure in the PR while still providing passing targeted tests for your change.
### Contributors Thanks to everyone who has contributed: [![Contributors](https://contrib.rocks/image?repo=Tencent/WeKnora)](https://github.com/Tencent/WeKnora/graphs/contributors) ## License This project is licensed under the [MIT License](./LICENSE). You are free to use, modify, and distribute the code with proper attribution.

repositories.name: dbdelve
repositories.description: Fast and lightweight DB Client made in Rust and GPUI.
repositories.readme: # DBDelve A fast, native, cross-platform, multi-engine database client. Written in Rust with GPUI, no Electron and no JVM: instant startup, friendly on your memory, and smooth scrolling through large tables where other clients crash or introduce limits. ## Community Ideas and discussion on [Discord](https://discord.gg/7PegWzwqCm). Like DBDelve? [Support its development](https://www.patreon.com/cw/ShayanAbbas1). Support is voluntary and does not provide any additional benefits. ![DBDelve in Gruvbox Dark Glass: a SELECT on the events table in the editor and its result grid below](assets/screenshots/query-dark.png) ![DBDelve in Gruvbox Light Glass: a join in the editor and its result grid below](assets/screenshots/query-light.png) Scrolling a million rows: https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/6e15d566-a110-46c6-a236-52af7d877d4c Launching, with the last results already there: https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/9e55da56-8577-43e0-812a-c77eb5d0e701 ## Why I wanted something which is performant, modern and consumes little ram. The existing DB clients are either filled with bloat (Electron and JVM) or paid. This is an alternative to them. No feature is ever going behind a paywall and with time we will have complete parity on features with those too. ## Install **macOS** (Apple Silicon, macOS 12 or later): ```sh brew install --cask ShayanAbbas1/dbdelve/dbdelve ``` The app isn't notarized, so the cask clears the quarantine flag macOS would otherwise refuse it over. Without Homebrew: ```sh curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ShayanAbbas1/dbdelve/main/install.sh | sh ``` **Linux** (x86_64 or aarch64): the same one-liner installs it under `~/.local` with no root, or `yay -S dbdelve-bin` from the AUR, or the tarball or AppImage from [the latest release][releases]. **Windows** (x86_64): run the installer from [the latest release][releases], or unzip the zip and run `dbdelve.exe`. The installer asks for AppData (just for you) or Program Files (all users). Updating, the `.dmg`, Linux requirements, building from source and where your data lives are all in [docs/install.md](docs/install.md). [releases]: https://github.com/ShayanAbbas1/dbdelve/releases/latest ## Supported databases Postgres, MySQL, MariaDB, SQLite, Turso, DuckDB, Snowflake, SQL Server, MongoDB, Redis (and Valkey, KeyDB, Dragonfly) and ClickHouse. Any other database with an ODBC driver is reachable through the bundled ODBC bridge, with that driver installed: IBM Db2, Oracle, SAP HANA, SAP ASE (Sybase), Informix, Teradata, Vertica, Exasol, Firebird, Amazon Redshift, Google BigQuery, Databricks, Apache Hive, Trino and Presto, Dremio, InterSystems IRIS, Microsoft Access and more. Grid editing is off, and statements you type run under the connection's mode. See [Connecting through ODBC](docs/odbc.md). ![The welcome screen: paste a connection URL or pick one of the engines, import from DBeaver or TablePlus, or pick a theme](assets/screenshots/welcome.png) ## What it does - **Make it yours.** The app's own themes alongside Catppuccin, Tokyo Night, Gruvbox and Dracula, each in dark, light and glass. Import themes from Zed or VS Code, or [write your own](docs/themes.md). ![The theme picker, with themes imported from Zed and VS Code and the import commands below them](assets/screenshots/themes.png) - **Bring your connections with you.** Import every saved connection, passwords and SSH settings included, from DBeaver, or TablePlus on macOS. - **Organize your connections into projects,** and jump to any of them from the palette, or disconnect back to a home screen that lists them all. ![The palette scoped to connections, grouped into two projects, with the current connection marked](assets/screenshots/projects.png) - **Never mistake prod for staging.** Every connection is isolated and can color the title bar. Run it read-only, read-write or with full access, and DBDelve asks before anything destructive. ![The connection form, grouped into connection, security and behaviour, with a color and a project for the connection](assets/screenshots/connection-form.png) - **Edits you can read first.** Change a cell and DBDelve writes the `UPDATE` for you to check before it runs. - **Keep the columns you need.** Hide or pin columns, and the layout survives a restart. - **Read a row in full** in the row panel, with JSON highlighted, and edit long values there. ![A table open in the grid, with the row panel showing one row's values and its JSON highlighted](assets/screenshots/table-dark.png) - **Import rows** from CSV, TSV or JSON, with every row checked and every statement shown before anything runs. ![Importing events.csv: format options on the left, each file column mapped to a table column, and a preview of the rows](assets/screenshots/import.png) - **Open a data file** by dropping it on the window: a CSV, Excel, Parquet or JSON file opens in DuckDB, held in memory, as a query you can change. A `.sql` file opens in a new query tab on the connection you're on, and runs only when you run it. - **See the query plan** highlighted in its own pane, with bad row estimates called out. ![An Explain Analyze plan for a join: each node with its actual and estimated rows and time, and a ×76 misestimate flagged](assets/screenshots/query-plan.png) - **Completion that knows your schema:** tables, and a table's columns after its name and a dot. ![Completing accounts. to its columns in a join](assets/screenshots/completion.png) - **Keyboard-first.** One palette for commands, tables, saved queries, history and connections, and every shortcut rebindable. - **Your SSH, not a reimplementation.** Tunnels run through your own `ssh`, so your config, agent and hardware keys just work. For Postgres, a Host that is a directory (`/var/run/postgresql`) reaches that Unix socket on the SSH host, optionally as another user (Run as); the server needs `socat`, and passwordless `sudo` for it when Run as is set. TLS modes other than `disable` and `prefer` are refused there. - **Sign in with a short-lived token.** On Postgres, MySQL, MariaDB, SQL Server, Redis and ClickHouse, a profile's Password command prints the password at every login, so cloud IAM auth keeps working after the token expires. For Amazon RDS: ```sh /opt/homebrew/bin/aws rds generate-db-auth-token --hostname %HOSTNAME% --port %PORT% --username %USERNAME% --region ``` `%HOSTNAME%`, `%PORT%` and `%USERNAME%` are the profile's own. DBDelve quotes them itself, so write them unquoted: one inside quotes stops the command from running. Give the program's full path (`which aws` prints it): an app opened from the Finder or a desktop launcher does not see the PATH your shell sets. Expires after reuses the output for that many seconds, in memory only; blank runs the command at every login. Free and open source, nothing behind a paywall, and no telemetry: the only request DBDelve makes on its own is an update check, which you can turn off. ## Benchmarks DBDelve 0.3.6 against DBeaver 25.3.1 on the same Postgres table, median of 5 runs each (2026-10-11, M1 Pro, 32 GB): | | DBDelve | DBeaver | | ----------------- | ------- | ------- | | Launch | 1.1 s | 5.2 s | | Idle memory | 133 MB | 606 MB | | 1,000-row query | 0.21 s | 1.96 s | | 1M rows, time | 56 s | 208 s | | 1M rows, memory\* | 4.9 GB | 17 GB | \* The whole 1M-row table pulled into memory on purpose, with the row limit off. Method and full results in [BENCHMARKS.md](BENCHMARKS.md). ## Logs and bug reports DBDelve keeps a diagnostic log on your machine and never sends it anywhere. To attach it to an issue, use **Help → Copy Diagnostics** and paste; **Help → Open Logs Folder** shows the files. If the default log doesn't show the problem, turn on **Verbose logging** in Settings and reproduce it. Read a log before you post it and remove anything sensitive. A verbose one can hold hostnames, database names and anything a database driver logs. ## License Copyright (C) 2026 Shayan Abbas and contributors, licensed under the [GPL-3.0](LICENSE). Code contributed before the switch was released under the [MIT License](licenses/MIT-dbdelve.txt), and that notice still applies to it. Third-party font and theme licenses are in [NOTICES.md](NOTICES.md).

repositories.name: LoopForge
repositories.description: Self-hosted workflows for coding-agent delivery. Orchestrate CodeBuddy, Codex and Claude Code with scripts and human approval gates. Includes Local workflows for coding assistants.
repositories.readme:
English · 简体中文

Two ways to work · Quick start · SOPs · Features · Local · FAQ · Docs

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/8af401d9-1aae-427c-b4bc-455c12d17beb

80-second product tour (1080p, with sound).

**LoopForge** is a self-hosted workspace where your team ships software with coding agents. Describe what you need to **Main Bot** in chat: it opens a Docker sandbox, checks out your repositories, delegates to project roles, and opens the PR. When a way of working proves itself, save it as an **SOP** (a standard workflow of agents, scripts and human gates) so the next requirement is delivered the same way, with review and approval built in. CodeBuddy, Codex and Claude Code do the work. LoopForge adds the roles, sandboxes, checkpoints and history around them, all on your own infrastructure under the MIT license. ## Two ways to work | | **Chat with Main Bot** | **Run an SOP** | | --- | --- | --- | | Best for | Exploring, quick fixes, iterating with the agent | Repeatable delivery with fixed stages and sign-off | | How it runs | Main Bot opens a [conversation workspace](docs/conversation-workspaces.md) (a Docker sandbox with your repos) on demand and calls project roles as subagents | The engine runs Agent, Script, Human-gate and sub-SOP nodes in order, in their own sandbox | | You stay in control by | Queuing or steering messages mid-reply, and pausing, resuming or taking over a running SOP from chat | Approving at human gates, sending work back to a chosen step, retrying or rerunning from any node | | Delivers | A PR/MR, or a direct merge into a shared branch (`mode=direct`) | Documents, code or a PR, plus per-node artifacts and logs | Both paths track the same **requirements**, so every change, whether made in chat or by an SOP, links back to what was asked for and counts toward delivery and cost reports.

The chat home. Type a request, @ a role, skill, requirement, SOP or repository, and pick the executor, model and permission mode per conversation.

## Why LoopForge Ask a coding agent to "fix this bug" and the result depends on that run. It might skip the plan, forget the tests, review its own code, or stop halfway without anyone noticing. That's fine for a demo, but it isn't how a team ships. - **Repeatable.** Same SOP, same stages, same checks for every requirement. Start from built-in backend, frontend, bug-fix and product SOPs. - **Separated roles.** Planning, implementation, review and testing each get their own prompt, executor, model, rules, Skills and MCP tools. A role works as an SOP node or as a subagent in chat. - **Human in the loop.** Approval gates where they matter. Read the report, approve, or send the work back to a chosen step. - **Observable and resumable.** Node status, tool traces, logs and artifacts in one place. Pause, retry a failed step, or rerun from any node. - **Your stack, your servers.** CodeBuddy, Codex or Claude Code as executors. GitHub, Skills and MCP as tools. Docker sandboxes or your own machine as the runtime. ## Quick start Install **Git** and clone the repository first. The installer checks Docker, Compose, Python 3 and curl and offers to install missing components. Python/curl installation supports apt, dnf and yum on Linux; the Compose plugin supports x86_64/arm64 and verifies the official release SHA-256. macOS needs a working Python 3 and Docker Desktop; Homebrew can install missing components. Ordinary Linux users are supported through Docker group access or sudo. Set `LOOPFORGE_YES=1` to accept installation prompts. Package and image downloads require internet access. ```bash git clone https://github.com/Tencent/LoopForge.git cd LoopForge ./start.sh ``` `./start.sh` pulls the GHCR release image pinned in `compose.yaml` without building locally (`bash scripts/install.sh` does the same). It creates the MySQL and platform services, generates configuration and session secrets, and installs the built-in sandboxes, starter SOPs and welcome project. Host Go and Node.js installations are not required. Configure model API keys and GitHub authorization after startup. Use `./start.sh logs`, `stop`, `restart` or `pull` to manage it, and `./start.sh dev` to build the checkout from source. Open the address printed by the installer and create your account; the first one becomes the administrator. The service listens on `0.0.0.0:8090` by default. On a cloud host, the installer reads the public IP from the provider's metadata service and prints it; allow the port in your security group, or put an HTTPS reverse proxy in front. Restrict access to your own IP until the administrator account exists. The home page's quick-access guide walks you through adding a model key, connecting a repository and choosing an SOP. ### Try it without an API key New accounts join the **LoopForge demo project**, which includes an SOP made only of a script and a human gate: 1. Switch to the demo project, open **Templates**, and open **Platform check · script & approval**. 2. Click **Run SOP**. A real script writes a report, then the run waits for you at the approval step. 3. Approve it from **Needs review** or the run page, and watch the run continue to its final artifact. ### What you need for real work | I want to… | You need | | --- | --- | | Run the script + approval demo | Nothing | | Chat with Main Bot, generate a document or a new project | An API key for the selected executor | | Change an existing repository (in chat or via an SOP) and open a PR | Model credentials and a GitHub repository (connect GitHub in personal settings) |
More setup details: executors, GitHub, sandboxes, access model
- **Executors.** Pick **CodeBuddy, Codex or Claude Code** beside the home composer, then a model. Each executor uses its own credentials from personal settings, and every SOP role can choose its executor independently (built-in roles default to CodeBuddy). Requirement clarification and AI notification summaries currently use CodeBuddy; scheduled assistant tasks run on the CLI the task selects. The Docker image ships CodeBuddy and Codex; Claude Code installs from npm on first use and is cached, so that first run requires npm access; [native deployments](docs/deployment.md#workers-and-runners) need the CLI for the executor you choose. - **GitHub is optional.** All built-in generic SOPs run without a repository: product SOPs deliver documents, and new frontend/backend projects deliver source files in the task workspace. Bug fixes still need source code and reproduction details. Connect a repository when you work on existing code or want PRs. - **Delivering to a repository.** Choose **Connect GitHub** in personal settings, approve the device code on GitHub and pick your repository (the LoopForge OAuth App is built in; no PAT required, manual PAT entry still works). Set executor credentials (or bind a local execution machine), then either run a project SOP or ask Main Bot to change the code and submit a PR/MR. - **Sandboxes.** In the default Compose installation, SOP runs and conversation workspaces both use Docker sandbox containers started through the host Docker socket. Default sandboxes reuse the installed runtime image, so nothing extra is built after installation; custom Dockerfiles still build their own images. Docker socket access grants control of the host daemon, so this setup is for trusted teams, not untrusted multi-tenant isolation. See [deployment boundaries](docs/deployment.md#accounts). Re-running the installer keeps your data. - **Accounts and access.** New installations listen on all interfaces (existing bind settings are kept) and are designed for a trusted team: signed-in users can read project data across the instance, and teammates can sign up from the login page (`AGENTFLOW_ALLOW_SIGNUP=false` in `.env` turns that off). Read the [account and access model](docs/deployment.md#accounts) before exposing it beyond your team. - **Remote access, HTTPS, separate workers.** See [Deployment](docs/deployment.md). - **Hacking on LoopForge itself?** `bash scripts/dev.sh` runs it natively (Go 1.26.11+).
## How SOPs work An **SOP** is the workflow a delivery follows. Agents, scripts and people take part in the same run:

The SOP designer with the built-in bug-fix SOP. Each step picks a role; failed checks can send the work back to an earlier step.

| Node | What it does | | --- | --- | | **Agent** | A role (prompt, executor, model, rules, Skills and MCP tools) that designs, implements, reviews or tests. | | **Script** | A deterministic shell step: build, test, lint, generate a report. No AI where AI is not needed. | | **Human gate** | Pauses the run until someone checks the artifacts and approves, or sends the work back to a step. | | **Sub-SOP** | Runs another SOP as a sub-workflow. | | **Preview build** | Builds a static site and archives it for review. | Each node declares its artifacts and dependencies, and the engine starts each step once its dependencies complete. Start from a built-in SOP, adapt its roles, rules and environment to your project, and publish versions as it evolves.

A run waiting at a human gate: approve and continue, add context and rerun the step, or send the work back upstream.

**A delivery we actually ran:** four CodeBuddy roles planned a Python fix, implemented it, reviewed it independently and summarized the delivery. Three real tests passed; the run waited for human approval, then verified the accepted code had not changed. The [reusable acceptance case](e2e/api/45-delivery-model.test.mjs) checks the files and results. See the [validation record](docs/validation.md) for scope and known gaps. ## Features | Area | What you get | | --- | --- | | **Chat workbench** | Main Bot with per-conversation executor, model and permission mode. `@` references for roles, skills, requirements, SOPs and repositories. Messages queue while a reply runs; *Steer* interrupts and sends now. Generated files open in a side panel with preview, source and download. | | **Conversation workspaces** | On-demand Docker sandboxes with the project's repositories checked out, project roles as native subagents, and direct control of a running SOP workspace: pause, resume or take over. | | **SOP designer** | Visual canvas with Agent, Script, Human gate, Sub-SOP and Preview nodes, rework-on-failure edges, validation, version history and publishing. Built-in backend, frontend, bug-fix and product SOPs. | | **Roles** | Reusable definitions: prompt, executor, model, rules, Skills, MCP tools, artifacts and gates, shared across SOP nodes and chat subagents. | | **Requirement → delivery** | Requirements tracked end to end, whether shipped by an SOP or straight from chat, with PR/MR status tracking, merge detection and direct-branch merges. | | **Runs & approvals** | Live node status, tool traces, worker logs, per-node artifact snapshots and workspace previews. A single **Needs review** inbox for every gate waiting on you. | | **AI scheduled tasks** | Recurring agent tasks with full workspace, SOP and MCP access; a shared market of versioned, parameterized task templates; automatic SOP dispatch for new requirements. | | **Insights & cost** | Engineering metrics, business-domain reports with static HTML/SVG export, and token/cost accounting for SOPs and conversations at public list prices. | | **Execution environments** | Platform workers, Docker sandboxes, or a connected local execution machine using your own tools and repositories. | | **Team-ready** | Password accounts, projects and members, light/dark/system themes, an OpenAPI-described HTTP and MCP API. Management pages are in English and Chinese; the chat workbench is Chinese for now. |

Built-in SOPs are read-only blueprints; copy one into your project to run and edit it.

## LoopForge Local Don't want to run a server? **LoopForge Local** brings the built-in delivery workflows straight into the coding assistant you already use: ```bash # Run inside your target project, e.g. for Claude Code npx -y loopforge-cli@latest install claude ``` Then run `/start-devflow ""` in Claude Code. | Host | Supported | | --- | --- | | Claude Code · CodeBuddy · Codex · Cursor | Classic (default) and Portable editions | | Pi | Portable edition | | DeepSeek Harness | Portable edition | | Hermes Agent | Portable edition | See the [local guide](docs/local/usage.md) for each host's entry point and [editions](docs/local/editions.md) for the differences. Source lives in [`local/`](local/). Local runs the built-in workflows today; exporting a platform SOP for standalone local execution is planned. | | Platform | Local | | --- | --- | --- | | Best for | Teams sharing chat workspaces, SOPs, approvals and history | One developer inside an IDE or CLI | | Needs | Docker + Python 3 | Node.js 20+, Python 3.8+ and a coding assistant | | Workflows | Chat with Main Bot + custom SOPs on a visual canvas | Built-in Classic / Portable workflows | | Evidence | Shared run details, approvals and metrics in the web workspace | Artifacts under `artifacts/{task_slug}/` + optional local dashboard | ## FAQ **Do I need an API key to try it?** No. The demo SOP uses only a script and a human gate. Chat and agent steps need a key for the executor you pick. Model usage is not included; you bring your own credentials. **Do I need GitHub?** No. Chat, documents and new projects run in the task workspace. Connect GitHub when you want to change an existing repository or open PRs. **Should I use chat or an SOP?** Use chat to explore and iterate; Main Bot can still open a PR. Once you find a way of working you want every requirement to follow, with fixed reviewers, tests and sign-off, put it in an SOP. Main Bot can start, pause and take over SOP runs, so the two paths work together. **How is this different from Dify, n8n or Flowise?** Those are general-purpose AI and automation workflow builders. LoopForge is built for **software delivery with coding agents**: implementer and reviewer roles, Docker sandboxes with real repositories, GitHub delivery, human acceptance gates and run evidence. **How is this different from using Claude Code, Codex or CodeBuddy directly?** LoopForge doesn't replace them; it orchestrates them. Each agent step and each chat turn runs one of those CLIs. LoopForge adds what surrounds it: who does what, in which sandbox, in which order, with which checks, and who signs off. **Is it safe to expose on the internet?** New installations listen on all interfaces and target a trusted team. Read the [account and access model](docs/deployment.md#accounts) and set up HTTPS before opening it up. Report vulnerabilities privately via the [security policy](SECURITY.md). ## Documentation | I want to… | Start here | | --- | --- | | Deploy, manage accounts, connect execution machines | [Deployment](docs/deployment.md) | | Understand chat workspaces, scheduled AI tasks and token pricing | [Conversation workspaces](docs/conversation-workspaces.md) · [AI scheduled tasks](docs/ai-scheduled-task-capabilities.md) · [Token pricing](docs/token-pricing.md) | | Install local workflows or choose an edition | [LoopForge Local](docs/local/usage.md) · [Editions](docs/local/editions.md) | | Extend the platform or use the HTTP / MCP API | [Architecture](docs/architecture.md) · [API reference](docs/api/README.md) · [Shared schedules API](docs/api/shared-schedules.md) | | Contribute to the UI | [Frontend design conventions](design.md) (Chinese) | | Check functional coverage and release readiness | [Validation record](docs/validation.md) · [Acceptance matrix](docs/testing/acceptance-matrix.md) · [Release review](docs/release-readiness.md) | | Understand source provenance and maintenance | [Public scope](docs/open-source-scope.md) · [Upstream synchronization](docs/upstream-sync.md) | ## Community Scan the QR code to join the LoopForge community group. ## Contributing Issues and PRs are welcome: share a use case, report a bug, or improve workflows, integrations and the platform experience. Start with the [contributing guide](CONTRIBUTING.md). Security issues go through the [security policy](SECURITY.md). If LoopForge is useful to you, a star helps others find it. ## License [MIT](LICENSE). Third-party components keep their own licenses and notices; see [THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md](THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md).

repositories.readme:
Application to comfortably monitor your network traffic.
Cross-platform. Intuitive. Reliable. Translated in:
🇨🇳 🇩🇪 🇫🇷 🇷🇺 🇵🇹 🇪🇦 🇮🇹 🇵🇱 [+ 18 more languages](https://github.com/GyulyVGC/sniffnet/issues/60)

## _Support Sniffnet's development_ 💖 Sniffnet is completely free, open-source software which needs lots of effort and time to develop and maintain. If you appreciate Sniffnet, [sponsor the project](https://github.com/sponsors/GyulyVGC) to support its [growth](https://github.com/GyulyVGC/sniffnet/blob/main/ROADMAP.md). For sponsorship inquiries, feel free to reach out at `sponsor@sniffnet.app`. A special shout-out to these awesome organizations and folks who are sponsoring Sniffnet:

Processing over 3TB/s of video at peak load, now hiring in SF

                 

## Download
x64 | arm64 | x86
Intel | Apple silicon
DEB: amd64 | arm64 | i386 | armhf
RPM: x86_64 | aarch64
AppImage: amd64 | arm64 | i386 | armhf
Links in the table above will download the latest version of Sniffnet directly from [GitHub releases](https://github.com/GyulyVGC/sniffnet/releases).
Not what you're looking for? Check out [alternative installation methods](https://github.com/GyulyVGC/sniffnet/wiki/Alternative-installation-methods). > [!NOTE] > > Remember to also install the [required dependencies](https://github.com/GyulyVGC/sniffnet/wiki/Required-dependencies) for your operating system. ## Features - 💻 choose a **network adapter** of your PC to inspect - 🏷️ select a set of **filters** to apply to the observed traffic - 📁 **import** and **export** comprehensive capture reports as **PCAP** files - 📊 view overall **statistics** about your Internet traffic - 📈 view **real-time charts** about traffic intensity - 🏠 identify connections in your **local network** - 🌍 discover the **geographical location** of remote hosts - 🌐 find out **domain name** and **ASN** of the hosts you are exchanging traffic with - 📖 identify **6000+ upper layer services**, protocols, trojans, and worms - 🎮 see which **programs** are generating network bandwidth - ⭐ save your **favorite** network hosts, services, and programs - 📌 keep an eye on your network even when the application is **minimized** - ️🔎 search and **inspect** each of your network connections in real time - 🔉 set custom **notifications** to inform you when defined network events occur - 🚫 import custom **IP blacklists** to highlight potentially dangerous connections - 🎨 choose the **style** that fits you the most, including custom themes support - ...and more! ## User manual Do you want to **learn more**?
Check out the [**Sniffnet Wiki**](https://github.com/GyulyVGC/sniffnet/wiki), a comprehensive manual to help you thoroughly master the application from a basic setup to the most advanced functionalities.
The Wiki includes step-by-step guides, tips, examples of usage, and answers to frequent questions.

## Troubleshooting
See details ### Missing dependencies Most of the errors that may arise are likely due to your system missing dependencies required to correctly analyze a network adapter.
Check the [required dependencies page](https://github.com/GyulyVGC/sniffnet/wiki/Required-dependencies) for instructions on how to proceed depending on your operating system. ### Rendering problems In some circumstances, especially if you are running on an old architecture or your graphical drivers are not updated, the `wgpu` default renderer used by [iced](https://github.com/iced-rs/iced) may manifest bugs (the interface glitches, color gradients are unsupported, or some icons are completely black).
In these cases you can set an environment variable to switch to the `tiny-skia` renderer, a CPU-only software renderer that should work properly on every environment: ```sh ICED_BACKEND=tiny-skia ``` ### ***In any case, don't hesitate to [open an issue](https://github.com/GyulyVGC/sniffnet/issues/new/choose), and I will do my best to help you!***
## Acknowledgements - A big shout-out to [all the contributors](https://github.com/GyulyVGC/sniffnet/blob/main/CONTRIBUTORS.md) of Sniffnet! - The graphical user interface has been realized with [iced](https://github.com/iced-rs/iced), a cross-platform GUI library for Rust focused on simplicity and type-safety - IP geolocation and ASN data are provided by [MaxMind](https://www.maxmind.com) - Free code signing for Windows Installer is provided by [SignPath.io](https://about.signpath.io/), certificate by [SignPath Foundation](https://signpath.org/) - [Sniffnet](https://ads.fund/token/0xadfc251f8ef00ceaeca2b5c1882dabe5db0833df) project is supported by ADS.FUND - Last but not least, thanks to [every single stargazer](https://github.com/GyulyVGC/sniffnet/stargazers): all forms of support made it possible to keep improving Sniffnet! ## Stay in the loop Wait... there's more!
Sniffnet is rapidly evolving, and new features are added on a regular basis.
Follow the news and Sniffnet socials to never miss an update.
You can also reach us by email at `info@sniffnet.app`.

repositories.name: substrate
repositories.description: Agent Substrate: the core system
repositories.readme:
# Agent Substrate **Zero-trust sandboxing for millions of agents on Kubernetes.** [![License](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-Apache_2.0-blue.svg)](https://opensource.org/licenses/Apache-2.0) [![Release](https://img.shields.io/github/v/release/agent-substrate/substrate)](https://github.com/agent-substrate/substrate/releases) [![CI](https://github.com/agent-substrate/substrate/actions/workflows/pr-workflow.yaml/badge.svg?branch=main)](https://github.com/agent-substrate/substrate/actions/workflows/pr-workflow.yaml?query=branch%3Amain) [![govulncheck](https://github.com/agent-substrate/substrate/actions/workflows/govulncheck.yaml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/agent-substrate/substrate/actions/workflows/govulncheck.yaml) [![GitHub stars](https://img.shields.io/github/stars/agent-substrate/substrate?style=flat)](https://github.com/agent-substrate/substrate/stargazers) [Quickstart](#quickstart-development) · [Security](docs/security/security.md) · [Architecture](docs/concepts/architecture.md) · [Contributing](CONTRIBUTING.md)
## What is Agent Substrate? Agent Substrate is a security-hardened, zero-trust runtime for sandboxed agents, engineered to safely run millions of agents and tools with 10x higher density than standard containers. Purpose-built for the era of autonomous agents, Substrate delivers fast resume operations in less than 500ms, with more than 500 activations per second. Agents get isolated compute, identity, networking, and storage. Sensitive credentials are kept out of reach from untrusted code. It supports multiple sandbox technologies, including microVMs and gVisor, while enabling a consistent lifecycle and management of all sandboxes. At its core, Agent Substrate maps a larger set of “actors” (stateful workloads such as agents) onto a smaller pool of ready “workers”. Because agents spend most of their lives waiting on models, tools, or humans, Substrate snapshots idle actors out of memory and restores them when a request arrives. Substrate is a low-opinion runtime, not an agent SDK. The workloads it runs do not have to be AI agents, though autonomous, untrusted, mostly-idle agents are the target for its isolation and scheduling model. It runs on standard Kubernetes: Pods, autoscaling, NetworkPolicies. It adds agent-specific scheduling, snapshotting, identity, and network mediation. This allows agentic, inference, training, and reinforcement learning workloads to share one infrastructure plane. ## Security Model Substrate treats every actor as untrusted and mutually hostile, so tenants can share physical nodes without sharing a security boundary. Every control operates within the cold-start and resume budget. See the [Security Guide](docs/security/security.md) for the full list of security principles and threat model. * **Always sandboxed, VM-grade boundaries:** Every actor runs inside a dedicated [gVisor](https://gvisor.dev/) (`runsc`) or [Cloud Hypervisor](https://www.cloudhypervisor.org/) microVM sandbox with segregated compute, network, and storage. Plain Linux containers are not supported. * **Per-agent cryptographic identity:** Every active actor receives a short-lived [SPIFFE](https://spiffe.io/) X.509 certificate by default, and the egress gateway can mint per-actor JWTs on demand when an egress policy calls for one. Both carry the actor identity and atespace (the Substrate namespace grouping), and are designed to federate with external identity systems. * **Zero credentials in the sandbox:** Actors never hold actor identity JWTs/certs, API keys, or cloud tokens. The built-in egress gateway ([`atenet-egress`](docs/guides/egress-credential-injection.md)) injects credentials into approved outbound requests outside the sandbox, so a prompt-injected or compromised agent has nothing to exfiltrate. * **Default-deny networking:** Actors start with a private network stack, no inbound path except through the ingress router (`atenet-router`), no lateral actor-to-actor or control-plane access, and outbound traffic [restricted by the egress gateway](docs/guides/egress-traffic.md). * **Pluggable policy at the edge:** The egress gateway acts as an external Policy Enforcement Point (PEP) that is fully replaceable, allowing you to attach your own authorization, DLP, prompt-injection scanning, or cloud IAM policy engine without placing policy code inside the untrusted sandbox. ## Performance & Multiplexing [![Agent Substrate Demo](https://img.youtube.com/vi/ZEzkCFJkzjY/hq1.jpg)](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ZEzkCFJkzjY) *Watch the Agent Substrate cluster multiplex ~250 stateful actors across just 8 physical pods.* This demo highlights the core developer experience and "Agentic Infrastructure" capabilities of Substrate: 1. **Actor Teleport:** Suspend and resume actors onto any available worker in the pool, when needed. 2. **Full-State Persistence:** Working memory (RAM) and filesystem state are captured in snapshots and restored intact across hibernation cycles, without losing in-flight sessions or tool state. 3. **10x–30x Oversubscription:** Multiplex a large registry of stateful actors onto a small pool of warm worker pods, paying for compute only while an agent is actively thinking or executing a tool. To reproduce this demo in your own cluster, see the **[Counter Demo](demos/counter/README.md)**. For more walkthroughs, visit the **[agent-substrate YouTube channel](https://www.youtube.com/channel/UCN9PPqlTtVxlcpbQ-NWpfZQ)**. ## Star History ## Framework Agnostic & Compatibility Agent Substrate is **framework and agent harness agnostic**. Because it runs standard OCI container images inside gVisor or microVM sandboxes and enforces security outside the workload, it hosts agents built on any stack without SDK changes: * **Agent Development Kit (ADK):** Preserves session state across invocations as actor state. * **LangChain:** Drop-in execution environment for LangChain agents and tool calls. * **Claude Code, Codex, and Antigravity:** High-density, stateful coding environments that keep system and filesystem state across sessions while isolating untrusted code execution. * **Model Context Protocol (MCP):** Deploy sandboxed MCP servers as Substrate Actors with per-actor identity and egress controls. ## Ecosystem & Examples * **[Agent Executor](https://github.com/google/ax):** A distributed agent runtime that demonstrates building a secure, hyper-scalable agent harness on Agent Substrate (see the [announcement blog](https://cloud.google.com/blog/products/ai-machine-learning/agent-executor-googles-distributed-agent-runtime) and [integration guide](https://github.com/google/ax#2-deploy-the-control-plane)). * **[kagent](https://github.com/kagent-dev/kagent):** A CNCF Sandbox project and Kubernetes-native framework for building, deploying, and managing AI agents that uses Agent Substrate to run sandboxed, stateful agent workloads (see the [announcement blog](https://kagent.dev/blog/the-future-of-kagent)). ## Status and compatibility Agent Substrate has reached 1.0. We are committed to compatibility and stability of the public API, CLI, and configuration formats. We will continue to add new features, but we will not break existing APIs or configuration formats without a major version bump. See "Compatibility and schema evolution" in [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) for more details. ### Supported Kubernetes Releases Currently we aim to support the [latest stable release](https://kubernetes.io/releases/) of Kubernetes, and the previous minor release. ## Community For announcements, technical discussions, and community support, please join the **[ate-dev](https://groups.google.com/g/ate-dev)** Google Group. We host a weekly community meeting every Thursday from 10:00am - 11:00am PST. - Video call link: https://meet.google.com/uhq-cxvn-dhy - Or dial: (US) +1 253-289-6971 PIN: 787 664 574 59# - More phone numbers: https://tel.meet/uhq-cxvn-dhy?pin=9044088223662 - [Meeting notes](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1obSIvfcafLNniLYTQCcT2eCgxHqa2AQ3Ga7YTsju49s) for the weekly sync meeting - [Recordings and transcripts](https://drive.google.com/corp/drive/u/0/folders/1rX1S6vPxPrR8dA1lEBuBEXkGKjHtG-mL) of all community meetings We also have channels in the CNCF slack; [request an invite here](https://slack.cncf.io/) if you don't have access. - [#substrate-users](https://cloud-native.slack.com/archives/C0B6RCAJULW) to discuss using substrate. - [#substrate-dev](https://cloud-native.slack.com/archives/C0B6M3E2J3D) to discuss developing substrate. ## Developing Please see [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) for guidelines on contributing to the project. We welcome contributions of all kinds, but the project is VERY young. Our immediate focus is on building out the core system and demos, so we may not be able to review or merge contributions that don't align with those goals in the near term. ## Quickstart (Development) To quickly set up the complete environment: 1. Make sure you have [Go](https://go.dev/doc/install), [`kubectl`](https://kubernetes.io/docs/tasks/tools/), and [`docker`](https://www.docker.com/) installed and configured on your dev machine. We will automatically manage other dependencies via Go, including [`kind`](https://kind.sigs.k8s.io/). A Linux host that will run more than about a thousand sandboxes also needs a larger kernel neighbor table (`net.ipv4.neigh.default.gc_thresh1/2/3` = 4096/16384/32768); `hack/create-kind-cluster.sh` warns when the host is at the default of 1024. 2. Run the following steps: ```shell # create cluster and local registry hack/create-kind-cluster.sh # make ate-setup target the kind cluster; set this in every shell that runs # ate-setup, including for the demo walkthroughs export ATE_INSTALL_KIND=true # install Substrate go run ./cmd/ate-setup deploy ate-system --credential-provider='{"name":"k8s.io"}' \ --ingress-allowed-spiffe-ids=spiffe://cluster.local/ns/ate-system/sa/atenet-client # install counter demo go run ./cmd/ate-setup deploy demo counter # install kubectl-ate go install ./cmd/kubectl-ate # create a counter actor in the demo's atespace (--template names the # actor template, resolved in the actor's atespace) kubectl ate create actor my-counter-1 -a ate-demo-counter --template counter # serve a local proxy on port 8000 that sends requests to the actor through the # network router kubectl ate proxy actor my-counter-1 -a ate-demo-counter ``` > [!IMPORTANT] > `{"name":"k8s.io"}` deploys the bundled credential provider with an empty, > default-deny namespace policy. Before an actor can have a credential > injected, grant its atespace the namespaces whose Secrets it may read; see > [Enable it](docs/guides/egress-credential-injection.md#enable-it). 3. In a **separate terminal**, send an HTTP request to increment the counter: ```shell curl -X POST -i http://localhost:8000/ ``` ### Custom Setup and Deployment You can deploy or cleanup specific Agent Substrate components using the installation script. See `go run ./cmd/ate-setup` for all options. ```bash # Re-deploy only ate-apiserver of the ATE system go run ./cmd/ate-setup deploy apiserver # Delete everything (core system and all demos) go run ./cmd/ate-setup delete all ``` ### Tearing down local `kind` resources If you need to delete the local `kind` cluster and its registry (if it was created by `hack/create-kind-cluster.sh`): ```bash ./hack/delete-kind-cluster.sh ``` ### GKE Quickstart To deploy on Google Kubernetes Engine, follow the official [GKE Installation Guide](https://docs.cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/ai-ml/install-overview-substrate). It lists the prerequisites and gives the one-line installer command. The installer's source and detailed options are in [substrate-gke](https://github.com/ai-on-gke/substrate-gke). ## Demos We provide several sample applications demonstrating Agent Substrate's capabilities: 1. **[Counter Demo](demos/counter/README.md)**: A stateful Go HTTP server demonstrating state preservation across suspends/resumes, and on-demand actor resumption and routing via the Substrate router. 2. **[Sandbox Demo (Antigravity)](demos/sandbox/README.md)**: A secure, sandboxed execution environment (running Alpine Linux) that allows arbitrary shell execution while preserving filesystem state across sessions. 3. **[Claude Code Multiplex](demos/claude-code-multiplex/README.md)**: Demonstrates oversubscribing physical hardware by multiplexing multiple Claude Code agents onto a limited pool of workers. 4. **[Multi-Template](demos/multi-template/README.md)**: Two `ActorTemplate`s running different binaries share one `WorkerPool`, even though the templates live in different atespaces. 5. **[Request Parking](demos/parking/README.md)**: An oversubscribed pool where the router holds inbound requests until a worker frees up, instead of returning `503`. ### Documentation & Guides * [Architecture](docs/concepts/architecture.md): How the control plane, node supervisor, and networking stack fit together. * [API Configuration Guide](docs/reference/api-guide.md): Detailed reference for configuring WorkerPools, ActorTemplates, Secrets, and Volumes. * [Full CLI Documentation](docs/reference/kubectl-ate.md): Installation and usage for `kubectl-ate`. * [Glossary](docs/reference/glossary.md): Core terms (Actor, Atespace, ActorTemplate, WorkerPool, Worker, ate-api-server, atenet, atelet, ateworker) and how they relate. * [Integration Repositories](docs/project/integration-repos.md): Where integrations live, how their repositories are named, and how fixes flow back to core. * [Observability Guide](docs/guides/observability.md): Guide to actor logging, metrics, and distributed tracing. * [Extending Substrate](docs/security/extensibility.md): How to augment or replace the built-in ingress and egress gateways. * [Authentication Guide](docs/guides/authentication.md): Which credential people, pods and CI jobs should use with the Substrate API, and how to trust more JWT issuers. * [Actor JWTs](docs/guides/actor-jwts.md): What an actor JWT contains, how relying parties verify it, and how to rotate the signing key. * [Federating actor JWTs](docs/guides/actor-jwt-federation.md): Serve the actor JWT issuer publicly and set up a relying party outside the cluster to trust it. * [Rotating the actor JWT signing key](docs/guides/actor-jwt-key-rotation.md): The rotation steps, how long to wait between them, and replacing a compromised key. * [Egress Traffic](docs/guides/egress-traffic.md): Which protocols an Actor may reach the outside world with and which are blocked. * [Enabling man-in-the-middle (MITM) interception for Actor Egress policy](docs/guides/egress-trust-bundle.md): Egress policies such as header injection depend on MITM interception of Actor traffic. This guide explains how an Actor should be configured to enable interception. * [Request Parking](docs/concepts/request-parking.md): How the router parks requests through transient worker-pool saturation. * [Sandbox Asset Cache](docs/concepts/sandbox-asset-cache.md): How a node caches the sandbox binaries actors run on, decides which runtimes it needs, and evicts to a budget. * [Upgrade Runbook](docs/guides/upgrade.md): Upgrade a running install to a newer supported release, and roll back if needed. * [Node Storage](docs/guides/node-storage.md): How to give snapshot I/O its own disk. * [Security Guide](docs/security/security.md): Security overview, security principles, and threat modeling. * [Benchmarking Guide](docs/guides/benchmarking.md): Locust-based load tests, monitoring stack, and the orchestrated benchmark harness. ## Tour ### Commands * `cmd/ateapi`: The core control plane API server exposing gRPC endpoints to manage actor and worker lifecycles. * `cmd/atelet`: A node-level DaemonSet that supervises physical worker pods, coordinates snapshotting, and manages state transfers. * `cmd/atecontroller`: A Kubernetes controller that reconciles WorkerPool custom resources. * `cmd/ate-idp-server`: Serves the OpenID discovery document and key set that relying parties use to verify actor JWTs. * `cmd/atenet`: A combined networking controller providing Envoy routing and proxy sidecars. * `cmd/ateworker-gvisor`: An interior-pod helper running inside sandboxed worker pods to execute `runsc` checkpoint and restore commands. * `cmd/ateworker-microvm`: The microVM peer of `ateworker-gvisor`, running actors as cloud-hypervisor VMs. * `cmd/podcertcontroller`: A "polyfill" that provides Pod Certificate signers that will eventually ship in upstream Kubernetes (with different names). * `cmd/kubectl-ate`: A CLI tool for managing Agent Substrate resources. See its [README](docs/reference/kubectl-ate.md). * `cmd/benchmarking`: Synthetic workloads used by the load tests, including `glutton`, which consumes RAM, disk, and file descriptors on demand. * `demos/`: Sample applications demonstrating Agent Substrate capabilities.

repositories.name: ohmygame
repositories.description: The open-source studio for making games with AI. Your own one-person game studio. Everything you need to make games with AI, in one app. Game canvas.  Bring your own key.
repositories.readme:
The open-source studio for making games with AI.

English | 简体中文 | 日本語

Website · Docs · Community games · Changelog

Describe a game, and the agent designs it, makes the art, writes the code, plays it to check it works, and publishes it to a link anyone can open. Design docs, images, video, 3D, and audio live on one canvas next to the code, instead of across five different apps. > [!NOTE] > OhMyGame is in beta. Expect rough edges, and tell us what breaks. ## Download | Platform | Download | | --------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------- | | macOS (Apple silicon) | [OhMyGame for Mac](https://ohmygame.ai/download/mac) | | Windows (x64) | [OhMyGame for Windows](https://ohmygame.ai/download/windows) | Older builds and release notes are on [Releases](https://github.com/WhiteTowerAI/ohmygame/releases). The Windows build isn't code-signed yet, so SmartScreen may warn on first install. Intel Mac and Linux are [on the roadmap](https://github.com/WhiteTowerAI/ohmygame/issues). OhMyGame ships without a model. On first launch, connect a provider or a coding agent you already use: [first run](https://ohmygame.ai/docs/first-run/). ## Features - **Let the agent build the game.** The agent drafts the design doc, writes the code, runs the game in a live preview, then plays it and tries a fix when something breaks. - **One canvas for every asset.** Generate images, video, 3D models, animation, voices, sound effects, and music with AI, and keep them organized on one canvas, ready to use in your game. - **Publish to a link.** Anyone can play it in the browser, and it shows up in the [Community](https://ohmygame.ai/community/). A multiplayer game's rooms, and its players' sign-in, saves, and leaderboards, come with it. - **Extend it with plugins.** A plugin can teach the agent new skills, give it new tools, and add panels and project types to the app. Bundled plugins cover Godot, Unity, Unreal Engine, Blender, Aseprite, Tiled, and platforms like WeChat and Douyin Mini Games. Or [make your own](https://ohmygame.ai/docs/plugins/make/). - **Bring your own agent.** Run OhMyGame on Claude Code, Codex, or OpenCode, or on any of 40+ model providers with your own keys. No per-run credits. It works the other way too: use the canvas, media generation, and playtesting from your agent over MCP. [Models](https://ohmygame.ai/docs/models/) · [External agents](docs/external-agents.md) ## What you can make Three games our team made with OhMyGame:
Interactive film Island builder Deckbuilding roguelike
**Web games** (Phaser, Three.js, React Three Fiber) are the best place to start. **Interactive stories** cover visual novels, interactive films, and story games. **General games** work with any engine or stack. Web games can be **multiplayer**, from board and card games to realtime arenas, played online with friends with no server of your own. See [Multiplayer](docs/multiplayer.md). [Play what others made](https://ohmygame.ai/community/). ## Documentation Guides for using OhMyGame are at **[ohmygame.ai/docs](https://ohmygame.ai/docs/)**: [install](https://ohmygame.ai/docs/install/), [first run](https://ohmygame.ai/docs/first-run/), [models](https://ohmygame.ai/docs/models/), and [plugins](https://ohmygame.ai/docs/plugins/). Technical references live in this repo under [`docs/`](docs/README.md), such as the [runtime](docs/runtime.md), [coding agents](docs/coding-agents.md), [custom models](docs/custom-models.md), and the [plugin contract](docs/plugins.md). ## Build from source Requires [Bun](https://bun.sh) 1.4.2+ and Node.js 22.19+. ```bash git clone https://github.com/WhiteTowerAI/ohmygame.git cd ohmygame bun install --frozen-lockfile bun run dev # web renderer + local daemon bun run dev:desktop # or the Electron app ``` Builds from source send no telemetry. For branches, checks, and optional cloud setup, see [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md). ## Privacy Your projects and API keys stay on your machine, and prompts go straight to the providers you choose. You only need an account to publish. Release builds send usage data and crash reports, which you can turn off in **Settings → About**. See [logs and diagnostics](docs/diagnostics.md). ## Contributing Issues and pull requests are welcome. Branch from `dev` and open PRs against `dev`; `main` holds releases. repositories.name: cross-platform-llm-client
repositories.description: A unified cross-platform AI client supporting seamless transitions between standard cloud APIs and on-device, offline execution of custom and uncensored language models.
repositories.readme:
# PrivateLM

[![Live Web App](https://img.shields.io/badge/Live_Demo-Try_Web_App-02569B?style=for-the-badge&logo=flutter&logoColor=white)](https://ai-chat-orailnoor.web.app/)

A production-ready, cross-platform AI chat client built with Flutter. It unifies local on-device LLM inference (Android) with cloud API access, giving users full control over how their models run.

![Image generation tested on Moto G71 (Snapdragon), Oneplus 10r (Mediatek), Pixel 6A (Tensor), Poco F1 (Snapdragon), Samsung s23 (Snapdragon) 4 steps fast](PrivateLM.png)
_Image generation tested on Moto G71 (Snapdragon), Oneplus 10r (Mediatek), Pixel 6A (Tensor), Poco F1 (Snapdragon), Samsung s23 (Snapdragon) 4 steps fast_

![Generated on pixel 6 with 20 step](IMG_2390.png)
_Generated on pixel 6 with 20 step_

---

## What It Does

- **Local Inference on Android** — Download and run GGUF models directly on your phone using GPU-accelerated inference (Vulkan). No internet required after download.
- **Cloud API Fallback** — Seamlessly switch to OpenAI, Anthropic, Google Gemini, or Kimi (Moonshot AI) when you need more power or are on unsupported platforms.
- **Multimodal Chat** — Send text and images in conversations. Vision support works with both local models (Qwen2-VL) and cloud providers.
- **Persistent Sessions** — All chats and settings are stored locally via Hive. Nothing leaves your device unless you explicitly choose cloud mode.
- **Background Services** — Firebase Cloud Messaging integration for push updates and background task handling.
- **Smart Auto-Configuration** — On first launch, the app detects your device's RAM and recommends optimal context size and token limits automatically.
- **Task Management (in development)** — A task view for structured, multi-step AI workflows is being built. It is not available in the app yet.

---

## Technical Architecture

### Stack

- **Framework:** Flutter 3.x (Dart >=3.3.0)
- **State Management:** GetX
- **Local Storage:** Hive
- **Networking:** Dio + `package:http`
- **Background Execution:** `flutter_background_service` + `flutter_local_notifications`
- **Push Notifications:** Firebase Core + Firebase Messaging

### Inference Pipeline

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                        UI Layer                              │
│   ChatView / ModelView / ServerView / SettingsView          │
└──────────────────────────┬──────────────────────────────────┘
                           │
┌──────────────────────────▼──────────────────────────────────┐
│                    Controllers (GetX)                        │
│   ChatController · TaskController · ModelController         │
│   SettingsController · HomeController                       │
└──────────────────────────┬──────────────────────────────────┘
                           │
┌──────────────────────────▼──────────────────────────────────┐
│                      Services                                │
│  ┌─────────────────┐  ┌─────────────────┐  ┌─────────────┐ │
│  │ InferenceService│  │  CloudService   │  │DownloadSvc  │ │
│  │  (local GGUF)   │  │ (OpenAI/Claude/ │  │ (model dl)  │ │
│  │                 │  │  Gemini/Kimi)   │  │             │ │
│  └─────────────────┘  └─────────────────┘  └─────────────┘ │
│  ┌─────────────────┐  ┌─────────────────┐  ┌─────────────┐ │
│  │  HiveService    │  │ DeviceInfoSvc   │  │ExecutionSvc │ │
│  │  ( persistence) │  │  (RAM/GPU tier) │  │ (bg tasks)  │ │
│  └─────────────────┘  └─────────────────┘  └─────────────┘ │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

### Local Inference (Android)

The app uses `llama_flutter_android`, a custom Flutter plugin wrapping `llama.cpp` for ARM64 devices. At runtime it:

1. **Detects GPU capabilities** via Vulkan to determine offload layers.
2. **Selects thread count** based on device tier (ultra / high / mid / low).
3. **Loads the GGUF model** with progress streaming.
4. **Generates tokens** via `generateChat()` with native chat-template support (ChatML, Llama-3, Gemma, Phi).
5. **Falls back** to manual prompt construction if native templates fail.

Idle detection (5s) and hard timeouts (180s) keep the UX responsive even on underpowered hardware.

### Cloud Inference

`CloudService` normalizes four different API shapes into a single interface:

- **OpenAI** — standard `/v1/chat/completions`
- **Anthropic** — Messages API with separate system param
- **Google Gemini** — `generateContent` with inline image base64
- **Kimi** — OpenAI-compatible endpoint from Moonshot AI

API keys are stored in Hive and never transmitted anywhere except to the provider's endpoint.

### Cross-Platform Abstraction

Local inference is conditionally compiled:

- **Android** → `inference_android.dart` (full llama.cpp engine)
- **Web** → `inference_stub.dart` (cloud-only, local coming soon)
- **iOS** → `inference_android.dart` (full llama.cpp engine via Metal GPU)

The `InferenceService` exposes `supportsLocalInference` so the UI can hide local-model UI on unsupported platforms.

---

## Supported Platforms

| Platform | Local Inference | Cloud APIs | Notes                           |
| -------- | --------------- | ---------- | ------------------------------- |
| Android  | ✅ Yes          | ✅ Yes     | CPU offload via NEON; minSdk 28 |
| iOS      | ✅ Yes          | ✅ Yes     | Metal GPU acceleration          |
| Web      | ❌ No           | ✅ Yes     | Cloud-only (local coming soon)  |

### iOS / iPad (Installation via AltServer)
The iOS/iPad release is distributed as a sideloadable IPA file. Due to the RAM requirements for local models, iPad is the recommended iOS target, but it can be installed on iPhones.

Here is how you can install the app using AltStore and AltServer:

**Prerequisites:**
* Ensure **AltServer** is installed and running on your Mac or Windows PC.
* Your iOS device must be connected to the same Wi-Fi network as your computer, or connected directly via a USB cable.
* You must have **AltStore** successfully installed on your iOS device.

**Installation Steps:**
1. **Download the IPA:** Go to the [Releases](https://github.com/orailnoor/cross-platform-llm-client/releases) page on your iOS device (using Safari) and download the latest `PrivateLM-iOS.zip` package, extract it to get the `.ipa` file.
2. **Open in AltStore:**
   * Locate the extracted `.ipa` file in your device's "Files" app.
   * Tap the **Share** button and select **AltStore** from the list of apps.
   * *Alternatively*, you can open the AltStore app, go to the **My Apps** tab, tap the **"+" (plus)** icon in the top-left corner, and select the downloaded IPA file.
3. **Install:** AltStore will begin installing the app. You may be prompted to enter your Apple ID credentials if this is your first time.
4. **Enable Developer Mode:** On iOS 16 and later, ensure "Developer Mode" is enabled in your device's Settings (`Settings > Privacy & Security > Developer Mode`) to launch the sideloaded app.
5. **Launch:** Once installation is finished, PrivateLM will appear in the **My Apps** tab in AltStore and on your device's home screen!

*Note: Sideloaded apps via AltStore expire after 7 days, but AltStore will attempt to automatically refresh them in the background when connected to the same Wi-Fi as your computer running AltServer.*

---

## Build Configuration

### Prerequisites

- Flutter SDK >=3.3.0
- Android SDK (API 26+)
- JDK 17
- NDK (bundled with Android SDK)

### Android

```bash
flutter pub get
flutter build apk --debug
```

Release APKs require a stable signing key. Copy
`android/key.properties.example` to `android/key.properties`, fill in the
keystore values, and keep both the key and its backup. Android accepts an APK
upgrade only when it is signed with the same key as the installed APK.

```bash
cp android/key.properties.example android/key.properties
flutter build apk --release --split-per-abi
```

Never rotate the signing key between GitHub releases. The per-ABI APKs must
also keep increasing the build number in `pubspec.yaml`.

### iOS

```bash
flutter pub get
cd ios
pod install
flutter build ios
```

### Web

```bash
flutter pub get
flutter build web --release
```

---

repositories.readme:
# v2rayNG

A V2Ray client for Android, support [Xray core](https://github.com/XTLS/Xray-core) and [v2fly core](https://github.com/v2fly/v2ray-core)

[![API](https://img.shields.io/badge/API-24%2B-yellow.svg?style=flat)](https://developer.android.com/about/versions/lollipop)
[![Kotlin Version](https://img.shields.io/badge/Kotlin-2.4.0-blue.svg)](https://kotlinlang.org)
[![GitHub commit activity](https://img.shields.io/github/commit-activity/m/2dust/v2rayNG)](https://github.com/2dust/v2rayNG/commits/master)
[![CodeFactor](https://www.codefactor.io/repository/github/2dust/v2rayng/badge)](https://www.codefactor.io/repository/github/2dust/v2rayng)
[![GitHub Releases](https://img.shields.io/github/downloads/2dust/v2rayNG/latest/total?logo=github)](https://github.com/2dust/v2rayNG/releases)
[![Chat on Telegram](https://img.shields.io/badge/Chat%20on-Telegram-brightgreen.svg)](https://t.me/v2rayn)

---

## Download / 下载

Download the latest release here:

在这里下载最新版本：

[https://github.com/2dust/v2rayNG/releases](https://github.com/2dust/v2rayNG/releases)

> [!TIP]
> v2rayNG is the mobile version. For the desktop version, please visit the v2rayN \
> v2rayNG 是手机版，电脑版请访问 v2rayN
>
> https://github.com/2dust/v2rayN

---

### Geoip and Geosite

- geoip.dat and geosite.dat files are in `Android/data/com.v2ray.ang/files/assets` (path may differ on some Android device)
- download feature will get enhanced version in this [repo](https://github.com/Loyalsoldier/v2ray-rules-dat) (note: it needs a working proxy)
- latest official [domain list](https://github.com/Loyalsoldier/v2ray-rules-dat) and [ip list](https://github.com/Loyalsoldier/geoip) can be imported manually
- possible to use a third-party dat file in the same folder, like [h2y](https://guide.v2fly.org/routing/sitedata.html#%E5%A4%96%E7%BD%AE%E7%9A%84%E5%9F%9F%E5%90%8D%E6%96%87%E4%BB%B6)

More in our [wiki](https://github.com/2dust/v2rayNG/wiki)

### Geoip 与 Geosite

- geoip.dat 和 geosite.dat 文件位于 `Android/data/com.v2ray.ang/files/assets`（部分设备路径可能不同）
- 下载功能将获取该 [仓库](https://github.com/Loyalsoldier/v2ray-rules-dat) 中的增强版本（注意：此功能需要一个可用的代理）
- 最新官方 [域名列表](https://github.com/Loyalsoldier/v2ray-rules-dat) 和 [IP 列表](https://github.com/Loyalsoldier/geoip) 可手动导入
- 也可在同一文件夹中使用第三方 dat 文件，例如 [h2y](https://guide.v2fly.org/routing/sitedata.html#%E5%A4%96%E7%BD%AE%E7%9A%84%E5%9F%9F%E5%90%8D%E6%96%87%E4%BB%B6)

更多内容请见我们的 [wiki](https://github.com/2dust/v2rayNG/wiki)

---

## Development guide / 开发指南

### Note

- Android project under the V2rayNG folder can be compiled directly in Android Studio, or using the Gradle wrapper. But the v2ray core inside the aar is (probably) outdated.
- The aar can be compiled from the Golang project [AndroidLibV2rayLite](https://github.com/2dust/AndroidLibV2rayLite) or [AndroidLibXrayLite](https://github.com/2dust/AndroidLibXrayLite). For a quick start, read the guides for [Go Mobile](https://github.com/golang/go/wiki/Mobile) and [Makefiles for Go Developers](https://tutorialedge.net/golang/makefiles-for-go-developers/).
- v2rayNG can run on Android Emulators. For WSA, VPN permission needs to be granted via `appops set [package name] ACTIVATE_VPN allow`.

### 提示

- V2rayNG 文件夹下的 Android 项目可直接在 Android Studio 中编译，或使用 Gradle wrapper 编译。但 aar 内置的 v2ray core（可能）已过时。
- aar 可由 Golang 项目 [AndroidLibV2rayLite](https://github.com/2dust/AndroidLibV2rayLite) 或 [AndroidLibXrayLite](https://github.com/2dust/AndroidLibXrayLite) 编译而成。快速入门可参考 [Go Mobile](https://github.com/golang/go/wiki/Mobile) 指南和 [Makefiles for Go Developers](https://tutorialedge.net/golang/makefiles-for-go-developers/)。
- v2rayNG 可在 Android 模拟器上运行。对于 WSA，需要通过 `appops set [package name] ACTIVATE_VPN allow` 授予 VPN 权限。

---


## GPG Verification / GPG 签名校验

Release files are signed with GPG to verify authenticity and integrity, helping prevent mirror, ISP, or CDN hijacking.

发布文件已使用 GPG 签名，可用于校验文件真实性与完整性，预防镜像站、运营商或 CDN 劫持。

### Fingerprint / 公钥指纹

```text
7694 5E9F 3E9A 168F 8070 F195 805D 661C
134D FAF6 8903 C199 463C 31E5 AE90 3AE0
```

---

## Community / 社区

Telegram Group / Telegram 群组：

[https://t.me/v2rayN](https://t.me/v2rayN)

Telegram Channel / Telegram 频道：

[https://t.me/github_2dust](https://t.me/github_2dust)
